info.title: F5Sign API
info.description:
eIDAS-compliant electronic-signature API. **Pre-1.0 and evolving** — this spec is
the proposal we hand the frontend teams to ratify routes + response shapes together
(ADR-0022 §A3). Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` (ADR-0025).

**Authentication.** Every `/api` request presents a credential, with one declared
exception: `GET /api/doc.json` (this document) is public, because it reads nothing
tenant-scoped. There is no fallback and no other unauthenticated surface — the
exception is pinned by `RouteAuthnDeclarationTest`, which asserts the unauthenticated
route set is exactly that one. Machine routes take an integrator API key
as `Authorization: Bearer f5s_ak_…`, and **the key establishes the tenant** — scope
is never sent by the caller. Those routes also require `F5Sign-Declared-Subject`,
naming the human who triggered the request (or `f5s:none` when none did). The
recipient signing routes take one of two credentials instead, and which one is a
property of the route rather than of the caller. The emailed link (`signingToken`)
opens a signing session. Opening returns a short-lived **session credential**
(`sessionCredential`) plus a renewal credential, and the session credential — not the
link — is what admits the recipient read-model, the document bytes and the commit.
Renewal needs **both**: the expired session credential in the header and the renewal
credential in the body, so a client that has kept only one of the two cannot renew.
The route decides which credential is accepted, so presenting the wrong kind is
refused rather than tried against another verifier.

⚠ **The `X-Tenant-Id` and `X-Acting-User-Id` headers are gone.** They were
caller-asserted and unverified — a client chose its own tenant and named its own
user — and sending them now has no effect at all.

post.summary: Add a workflow step to a draft envelope
post.description:
Adds a step and says how much agreement it needs: `completion` `ALL` (the default) or `AT_LEAST` with `min_signatures`, an optional `veto` on `AT_LEAST`, and an optional `deadline_hours` counted from the step's activation. What depends on the recipients — a minimum below the step's blocking members, one blocking role per `AT_LEAST` step — is checked when the envelope is sent, since recipients are added after the step. 

⚠ **Two policies are accepted that wait longer than their authors usually expect.** An `AT_LEAST` step without a deadline waits for EVERY member, not only for `min_signatures` of them, so one that is not the last step should carry a deadline: otherwise one silent member keeps the next step from activating and the envelope ends not agreed at its expiry though the minimum was met. A `veto` step without a deadline resolves only at the envelope's expiry whenever a member stays silent, and closing the envelope early is refused until then. Give either a deadline unless waiting is what you mean. 

Re-sending the same ordinal with the same policy is a replay and answers 201 again; with a different policy it is refused with 409.

201.description: Created — the step ordinal (its client-facing handle for adding recipients).

409.description: The envelope is no longer a DRAFT — steps are authored before send, and a sent envelope is amended by voiding and reissuing it — or a step with this ordinal already exists asking for a different policy: re-sending an ordinal is a replay, not an edit.

post.summary: Add a recipient to a step of a draft envelope
post.description:
Adds a recipient and, optionally, declares the two authentication gates they must pass. 

⚠ **When the server generates an access code, `access_code` in the 201 body below is the only time it is ever disclosed.** It is stored as a peppered hash, so no endpoint can return it again and support cannot look it up — the recovery for a lost code is `POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/access-code`, which mints a *new* one and invalidates the old. Capture it from this response and pass it to the sender at once. 

It is also your responsibility from that point on: if your integration logs HTTP responses, this value lands in your logs, and nothing on our side can prevent or detect that. Exclude it, or redact this field.

201.description: Created — the new recipient id, plus the generated access code when there is one. `access_code` is present **only** when a gate declared `ACCESS_CODE` and no `access_code` was supplied in the request; a sender who chose their own already knows it, so it is not echoed. Absent on every other call, and never returned by any other endpoint or any later read.

access_code.description: The one-shot access code, shown here and nowhere else. Six digits, generated from a CSPRNG. Omitted from the body entirely when the server generated nothing.

400.description: Malformed body, or `INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER` — `phone` could not be read as a number at all, or names no assigned range. Distinct from the 422 below, which is raised about a number that is perfectly valid but cannot carry the declared method.

409.description: The envelope is no longer a DRAFT. Recipients are added before send; a sent envelope is amended by voiding and reissuing it.

422.description: The payload is well-formed but cannot be accepted. Beyond the ordinary field violations, `code` distinguishes two conditions worth branching on: `AUTH_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE` — the declared method is a real catalog member but this deployment has not wired a provider for it, so the same request would succeed elsewhere and the remedy is to choose another method rather than to fix the request; `RECIPIENT_CANNOT_RECEIVE_METHOD` — the method IS wired here, and this recipient, NOT declared claimable, has nowhere to receive it: OTP_EMAIL with no address, OTP_SMS with no phone, or OTP_SMS against a landline, which is a valid number that cannot receive a text. Three remedies: supply the missing contact, declare a method that needs none, or — when the party genuinely is not known yet — send `claimable: true` and name them at the claim. ⚑ **The qualification is the whole of it: on `claimable: true` this check is DEFERRED, not lifted.** A slot is authored with no occupant, so there is no contact to check yet and none of the three conditions above can refuse the call; the same check, with this same `code` and the same first-unreachable-method message, is re-run at `POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/claim` against the contact that call supplies. It is keyed on the DECLARATION and never on "has no contact yet": an ordinary recipient you leave contactless is refused here exactly as before. Refused HERE rather than when the signer is already waiting at a gate — on a paid channel the late failure is also a charge.

post.summary: Correct a recipient's contact details and re-send their invitation
post.description:
Replaces the contact details a recipient of a **sent** envelope is reached at — the email address, the phone number, or both — and re-invites them. Their `outcome` is untouched: it was already PENDING, since a closed leg cannot be corrected. What changes is `delivery`, and only for the destination you actually rewrite — correcting a phone keeps a bounce that is still true of the address. AT LEAST ONE of the two must be sent; a field you omit is left as it is, and there is no way to clear a contact here. The recovery from `delivery: FAILED`, and also usable when delivery reports nothing wrong — an address that is simply wrong often produces no detectable failure at all. Bounded to 3 corrections per recipient. The invitation follows the workflow: it is sent at once if this recipient's step is already active, and when their step opens otherwise — a correction never hands a later party their signing link ahead of turn.

⚠ If the address is right and the invitation was merely lost, ignored or filtered, use `POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/resends` instead. It re-invites without spending one of these 3 corrections and without recording a claim that the address was wrong.

204.description: Corrected — the recipient is back to PENDING at the new address, and a fresh invitation is on its way if their step is active (otherwise it is sent when their step opens). GET the envelope to observe the new outcome.

400.description: Malformed body, or `INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER` — the phone could not be read as a number at all, or names no assigned range. Distinct from the 422 below, which is raised about a number that is perfectly valid.

409.description: The correction cannot be applied. `code` distinguishes the reasons: `RECIPIENT_LEG_CLOSED` — this recipient already completed, declined, delegated or was skipped, so there is nothing left to deliver to them; `RECIPIENT_CORRECTION_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` — all 3 corrections are spent, and the remaining recovery is to void the envelope and reissue it; `RECIPIENT_SLOT_NOT_CLAIMED` — this recipient is a claimable slot nobody has claimed yet, so there is no named party to re-reach. Use POST /api/v1/envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/claim, which names the party and sets their contact in one recorded act; correcting is not the operation you want. A slot that HAS been claimed is an ordinary recipient and corrects normally; `CONFLICT` — the envelope is terminal, or has not been sent yet (nothing has been delivered, so there is nothing to correct); `ENVELOPE_EXPIRED` — its `expires_at` has passed, and its expiry closes it within a minute; do not retry, read the envelope again.

422.description: The body parses and a rule about its contents fails. `code` distinguishes: `RECIPIENT_CANNOT_RECEIVE_METHOD` — the corrected details cannot carry a method this recipient has declared, the usual case being a mobile corrected to a landline while OTP_SMS is declared. ⚑ A REFUSED correction spends none of the three, so fixing the number and retrying is free. `VALIDATION_ERROR` — the ordinary shape failures, including sending neither field.

post.summary: Mint a replacement access code for a recipient
post.description:
Replaces this recipient's access code and lifts any authentication lockout they are under, in one call. The previous code stops working immediately — but read the next paragraph before treating this as a way to lock somebody out. 

⛑ **A reset DOES evict a party who has already passed the gate — every session credential minted before this call is retired**, so anyone holding one is refused on the read-model, the document bytes and the commit. 

⚠ **Whether that is CONTAINMENT depends on which gate declares the code, and you must check.** The link is deliberately left working (see below), so an intruder can re-open it. If the recipient's **access** gate declares `ACCESS_CODE`, re-opening asks for the code and they are stopped at the door: this endpoint is sufficient on its own. If the access gate is **neutral** and the code sits on the **signing** gate, re-opening mints a fresh credential and they get the read-model and the document bytes back — only the signature is still blocked. For that configuration a reset contains the ACT and not the READS, and voiding the envelope is the only thing that closes both. 

⚑ **The signing link itself keeps working, and that asymmetry is deliberate.** Only the credential is retired; the emailed link still opens. The legitimate signer is expected back through that same link with the new code, so revoking it too would strand exactly the person this endpoint exists to serve. ⛔ A **contact correction** is the gesture that does revoke the link, because there the old address is the thing being disavowed. 

⛔ **Voiding is for a different question.** It closes the envelope without agreement for EVERY recipient — no further act is admitted from anyone — but it does not withhold reads from everyone: a recipient who had already signed, or who reads as informational, keeps passing the access gate and reads the sealed record once it lands; a decliner, or a released member who neither signed nor reads as informational, is refused instead (ADR-0073 §2.3, §2.15). Reach for it when the document should not be signed at all, not merely when one recipient's code leaked. 

⚠ **The new code is returned in this response and nowhere else.** It is stored only as a peppered hash — no endpoint can return it again, and support cannot look it up. If it is lost, the only remedy is to call this endpoint again. 

It is also your responsibility once received: if your integration logs HTTP responses, this value lands in your logs, and nothing on our side can prevent or detect that. Exclude it, or redact this field. 

Works on a DRAFT envelope as well as a sent one, and on a recipient who has never opened their link — those are the moments a sender reaches for it. Refused (`RECIPIENT_ACCESS_NOT_RECOVERABLE`) for a recipient who can no longer pass the access gate — a decliner, or a released member who neither signed nor reads as informational; a signer, even after the envelope has completed, and an informational member are never refused here.

200.description: Reset — the new code, disclosed here for the only time. Any lockout on this recipient is lifted; `auth.hard_locked` on the envelope read model reads false from now on.

access_code.description: The new access code. Six digits when the server generated it; the value you sent, echoed, when you supplied your own.

409.description: `RECIPIENT_ACCESS_NOT_RECOVERABLE` — this recipient can no longer pass the access gate (a decliner, or a released member who neither signed nor reads as informational): there is nothing an access code would admit them to. ⚑ That includes a blocking member who has not acted once their step has reached its deadline, from the deadline itself: the scheduled sweep releases them, or ends the envelope, up to a minute later, and this answer does not wait for it.

post.summary: Lift a recipient's authentication lockout
post.description:
Clears the lockout a recipient hit by failing their authentication too many times, leaving their access code unchanged. Use this when the signer still knows their code — a lockout is shared by everyone holding the link, so it is often spent by somebody else's guessing, and resetting the code would strand the legitimate signer a second time. Use `POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/access-code` instead when the code itself has been lost; that call lifts the lockout too. 

Takes effect on the signer's very next attempt. Safe to call on a recipient who is not locked out, and on one who has never opened their link — it is a no-op there rather than an error. Refused (`RECIPIENT_ACCESS_NOT_RECOVERABLE`) for a recipient who can no longer pass the access gate — a decliner, or a released member who neither signed nor reads as informational, including a blocking member whose step has reached its deadline without their act, before the sweep has recorded the release; a signer, even after the envelope has completed, and an informational member are never refused here.

204.description: Unlocked — the recipient may authenticate again immediately. GET the envelope to observe `auth.hard_locked` back at false.

409.description: `RECIPIENT_ACCESS_NOT_RECOVERABLE` — this recipient can no longer pass the access gate (a decliner, or a released member who neither signed nor reads as informational): there is nothing to unlock them into. ⚑ That includes a blocking member who has not acted once their step has reached its deadline, from the deadline itself: the scheduled sweep releases them, or ends the envelope, up to a minute later, and this answer does not wait for it.

post.summary: Send a recipient's signing invitation again
post.description:
Re-invites a recipient of a **sent** envelope at the address already on file, for the ordinary case of an invitation that was lost, ignored or filtered. Nothing about the recipient changes: the contact is untouched, the outcome is untouched, and — unlike `POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/corrections` — it spends none of that recipient's 3 corrections and records no claim that the address was wrong. Use `corrections` when the address really is wrong; use this when it is not.

The new email carries a **new** signing link. ⚠ The previous link is NOT cancelled: it keeps working until its own expiry, so a recipient who later finds the older message can still use it. Both links lead to the same signing session.

⚠ If the recipient is signing **right now**, the new link interrupts them: opening it issues fresh credentials and, where their envelope declares an authentication gate, sends them back through it. No progress is lost and it is the same session, but they will notice. There is no way to ask whether somebody is mid-ceremony before calling this.

Refused inside a short minimum interval since the last resend to the same recipient, so a retry loop cannot be turned into a mailing campaign. Resends are not limited by count.

204.description: Accepted — a fresh invitation is on its way to the address on file. The delivery itself is asynchronous, so a 204 means the resend was recorded, not that the mail has been handed to a provider yet.

409.description:
The invitation cannot be sent again. `code` distinguishes the reasons: `RECIPIENT_RESENT_TOO_RECENTLY` — one went out inside the minimum interval; this is the only refusal here that retrying later resolves. `RECIPIENT_STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` — this recipient's step has not opened, so they have never been invited and there is nothing to resend; their first invitation is sent automatically when their turn comes. `RECIPIENT_LEG_CLOSED` — this recipient already completed, declined, delegated or was skipped, so there is nothing left to deliver to them. `RECIPIENT_HAS_NO_ADDRESS` — this recipient carries no address, so there is nothing to send to; correct their contact rather than retrying. On an open step the correction re-invites at once; on a step that has not opened yet it takes effect and the invitation still waits for their turn. `ENVELOPE_EXPIRED` — the envelope's `expires_at` has passed, and its expiry closes it within a minute; there is nothing left to invite anyone to. `CONFLICT` — the envelope is terminal, or has not been sent yet (nobody has been invited, so there is nothing to resend).

With `code: RECIPIENT_RESENT_TOO_RECENTLY` — **and only that one** — the body carries `next_resend_at`, an RFC 3339 instant from which this recipient may be sent to again. It is absolute rather than a countdown so it survives the hop and does not depend on the two clocks agreeing. Show the time; do not compute a remaining interval from it and re-render the wait. No other code carries that member, because none of the others is cured by waiting.

post.summary: Claim a recipient slot — name the party it was authored without
post.description:
Fills a recipient slot that was deliberately authored with no occupant (`claimable: true` on the add call), naming the party and supplying the contact their declared gates need. 

⚑ **A fill, not a correction.** `POST .../corrections` changes where an ALREADY NAMED party is reached and cannot name anybody; this names the party, and it is refused on a recipient that was never declared claimable. The two are not interchangeable in either direction: a correction on a slot nobody has claimed is refused with 409 `RECIPIENT_SLOT_NOT_CLAIMED`. 

⚑ **A slot is filled ONCE, and retrying is safe.** Sending this call again with the same body returns the same `204` as the first — the two are deliberately indistinguishable, so a client that timed out and retried needs no special handling and must not branch on the difference. A field you OMIT on the retry is not compared, so a retry that leaves out a `locale` you sent the first time still converges. A body that CONTRADICTS the stored claim on a field it supplies is a re-assignment rather than a retry, and is refused with 409 `RECIPIENT_ALREADY_CLAIMED` naming the field that differed. 

The `F5Sign-Declared-Subject` header must name a person: a claim is an act somebody performs, so the reserved `f5s:none` — legal on every other endpoint — is refused here with 400.

204.description: Claimed — the slot now names this party and will not accept another. GET the envelope to observe it. ⚑ An identical replay of the same body answers 204 as well, and is deliberately indistinguishable from the first call.

400.description: Malformed body; or `INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER` — `phone` could not be read as a number at all, or names no assigned range (distinct from the 422 below, which is raised about a number that is perfectly valid); or `INVALID_DECLARED_SUBJECT` — the `F5Sign-Declared-Subject` header is not acceptable, which on THIS endpoint additionally covers the reserved `f5s:none`. Naming a party to a document is an act a person performs, so a claim that declares there is no triggering human is refused; send the reference your own system holds for the dispatcher who decided it. ⚠ THE TWO CASES ARE NOT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE BODY: a malformed header and the reserved `f5s:none` both answer this code with the same generic `detail`, because the shared handler suppresses value-object messages so a rejected value can never leak (some of them are personal data). Branch on the code and check the header you sent; do not parse `detail`. ⚠ We validate that a person was declared and do NOT store the reference — this endpoint does not build an audit trail of who claimed what.

409.description: The slot cannot be filled. `code` distinguishes the reasons, and they route to different screens: `RECIPIENT_NOT_CLAIMABLE` — this recipient was never declared claimable, so there is no open occupancy to fill and you probably have the wrong recipient id; a recipient named at authoring is changed nowhere, not here; `RECIPIENT_ALREADY_CLAIMED` — the slot is filled and this body names a DIFFERENT party, which is a re-assignment rather than a retry; the message names the field that diverged, and the slot keeps the party it already names; `RECIPIENT_CAN_NO_LONGER_ACT` — this recipient's leg is closed, or the step they sit on has completed, or that step's deadline has passed (judged at the instant of this call, even before the step is closed by it): there is nothing left for a claimed party to do, and naming one would record an addressee for an act that can never happen. The refusal is the property, not a list — a leg is closed on any TERMINAL outcome, of which COMPLETED, DECLINED, DELEGATED and SKIPPED are today's examples, and a new terminal outcome is covered the day it ships rather than the day this sentence is remembered. `ENVELOPE_EXPIRED` — the envelope's `expires_at` has passed, and its expiry closes it within a minute; do not retry, read the envelope again; `CONFLICT` — the envelope itself is in a state that admits no write: it is closed, whether it ended agreed or not.

422.description: The body parses and a rule about its contents fails. `code` distinguishes: `RECIPIENT_CANNOT_RECEIVE_METHOD` — what this claim supplies cannot carry a method this recipient DECLARED at authoring: OTP_EMAIL with no `email`, OTP_SMS with no `phone`, or OTP_SMS against a landline, which is a valid number that cannot receive a text. This is the check the add call deferred when the slot was marked claimable, re-run here against the contact you have now supplied, and it names the FIRST unreachable method in declaration order. ⚑ A REFUSED claim consumes NONE of the once-only fill, so fixing the body and retrying is free. `VALIDATION_ERROR` — the ordinary shape failures, including omitting `full_name`.

post.summary: Author a field of a draft envelope and every place it appears
post.description: Exactly one of `occurrences` / `anchor_text` must be supplied. Each occurrence names its own `document_id`, so one field may render several times, on one document or across several, sharing one definition and one value. A `SIGNATURE` field renders exactly once and additionally requires the recipient to already hold the `signs` grant on that document; all three refusals are 422. The field id is minted by the server and returned in the response — it is not accepted in the body, so a repeated POST authors a second field rather than converging on the first.

409.description: The envelope is no longer a DRAFT. Fields are authored before send; a sent envelope is amended by voiding and reissuing it.

post.summary: Assign a draft envelope's recipient to sign one document (grants signing and sight; use document-assignments to grant sight without signing, or signing without sight)

204.description: Assigned — idempotent when the same pair and placements are re-sent.

post.summary: Declare a draft envelope's per-recipient document access, in one batch

204.description: Declared. Atomic — a conflict on any item applies none of them. Idempotent when the same matrix is re-sent.

409.description: Either the envelope is no longer a draft — declarations are authored only while it is — or a pair was re-declared with different grants, or a signing pair with different placements. Declarations are append-only.

post.summary: Send a draft envelope (DRAFT → SENT)

204.description: Sent — the envelope is now SENT and its first step is active.

409.description: The envelope is not a DRAFT. It has already been sent, or it was voided; leaving DRAFT is one-way, so reissue rather than re-send.

422.description: The draft is not complete enough to send. Most conditions — no document, no step, a step with no recipient, a signer with nothing to sign, a field nobody can answer — carry the status default `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` and name the gap in `detail`. The step policies are judged here too, once the recipients are known, and each carries its own `code` (when several apply, `code` is the first and `detail` names them all): `STEP_MINIMUM_NOT_BELOW_MEMBERS` — an `AT_LEAST` step asks `min_signatures` equal to or above its blocking members; equal is unanimity, which has one encoding: send the step as `completion: ALL`; `STEP_MIXES_BLOCKING_ROLES` — an `AT_LEAST` step holds more than one blocking role (SIGNER and APPROVER); it counts one role, so split it into two steps (informational members beside it are fine); `ENVELOPE_HAS_NO_BLOCKING_MEMBER` — no recipient in any step is a SIGNER or APPROVER, so nothing could ever agree; `RECIPIENT_ROLE_NOT_BUILT` — a recipient is IN_PERSON_HOST or CERTIFIED_DELIVERY, roles with no ceremony yet.

post.summary: Void a live envelope, ending it without agreement

204.description: Voided — the envelope has closed without agreement (`outcome: NOT_AGREED`, `end_cause: SENDER_VOIDED`; idempotent if already closed that way). Recipients' live signing sessions are revoked, except those of a recipient who has already signed or who is informational (a viewer, for example): they keep theirs, because they may still read the document once it is sealed. No act is admitted from any session once the envelope has closed.

409.description: The envelope cannot be voided from its current status. Branch on `code`. `ENVELOPE_REACHED_AGREEMENT` — its agreement is already secured (`agreed_at`): every blocking recipient has signed under `ALL`, or the quorum has been reached under `AT_LEAST n`, so it completes on its own; read it again rather than retrying the void. `ENVELOPE_EXPIRED` — its `expires_at` has passed: from that instant only its expiry ends it, within a minute, as NOT_AGREED with `end_cause: EXPIRED` (or AGREED if its last step already has what it needs); read it again rather than retrying. `STEP_DEADLINE_PASSED` — the open step's deadline has passed and the scheduled sweep has not closed it yet (it runs every minute). The envelope cannot be voided or closed in that window, because the sweep decides how the step ended (ADR-0073 §2.12). Retry after a minute. The envelope will then either have ended, or have moved on to a later step. Any other 409 carries the bare `CONFLICT` code: the envelope is a DRAFT (discard it instead) or has already ended (COMPLETED).

post.summary: Close an envelope whose agreement is secured, releasing whoever is still pending

204.description: Closed — the envelope has closed agreed (`outcome: AGREED`, `closed_at` and `ended_by` set, `end_cause` null). Every recipient still pending is `RELEASED` with `released_by: SENDER_CLOSED`. `status` stays `SENT` until the signatures admitted before the close have landed, then `COMPLETED`. Idempotent: a repeat on an envelope already closed this way is another 204 and changes nothing.

409.description: The envelope was not closed. Branch on `code`. `ENVELOPE_AGREEMENT_NOT_SECURED` — its agreement is not secured yet (`agreed_at` is null): wait for `agreed_at` and close then; or void it instead. A step with a veto is secured only when it closes, so it cannot be closed early. `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` — it has already closed another way; `GET` it to read how it ended. `ENVELOPE_EXPIRED` — its `expires_at` has passed: from that instant only its expiry ends it, within a minute, as AGREED if its agreement is already secured, else as NOT_AGREED with `end_cause: EXPIRED`; read it again rather than retrying. `STEP_DEADLINE_PASSED` — the open step's deadline has passed and the scheduled sweep has not closed it yet (it runs every minute). The envelope cannot be voided or closed in that window, because the sweep decides how the step ended (ADR-0073 §2.12). Retry after a minute. The envelope will then either have ended, or have moved on to a later step. Any other 409 carries the bare `CONFLICT` code: the envelope is a DRAFT (discard it instead).

post.summary: Extend a sent envelope's life

200.description: Extended — the envelope now expires at `expires_at`. Repeatable, each time forward, up to 180 days after the send. A signing link still lives seven days from its invitation, so a recipient whose link has lapsed needs a resend to act in the added time.

409.description: The date was not moved. `code` names the condition: `ENVELOPE_NOT_SENT` — a draft holds its life in days (`expires_in_days`) and the send resolves the date; there is nothing to extend yet. `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` — the envelope has closed; nothing is left to wait for. `ENVELOPE_EXPIRED` — its `expires_at` has already passed: the expiry closes it within a minute, and nothing, an extension included, moves it before then. `EXPIRY_NOT_FORWARD` — the requested date is not after the current one. A retry of an extension that already landed (its `200` lost) is refused this way too, and nothing is applied twice: re-read the envelope's `expires_at` to tell the two apart. `EXPIRY_BEYOND_LIMIT` — the requested date is more than 180 days after the send.

get.summary: Download the sealed audit trail of an ended envelope

200.description: The sealed audit trail: a PDF/A-3a document with its data attached as JSON, sealed by the platform. It never changes once issued.

404.description: No audit trail for this envelope under your tenant. One answer for an unknown envelope, another tenant's, one that has not ended, and one whose trail is not issued yet. A trail is issued shortly after the envelope completes or is voided, so for an ended envelope a later request can succeed.

409.description: `AUDIT_TRAIL_UNAVAILABLE`: the trail is recorded, but its PDF cannot be read. A later request gives the same answer unless the platform restores the PDF, which it cannot do for a trail that was destroyed.

post.summary: Mint a recipient signing access token (sender-side)

token.description: The recipient's signing credential, opaque (ADR-0045). Returned exactly once and stored only as a digest, so it cannot be read back or resent — reissue instead. Put it in the invitation link as-is: it is URL-path-safe and must not be encoded or truncated. Valid for 7 days from issuance.

404.description: No such envelope, it belongs to another tenant, or that recipient is not on it — one indistinguishable answer, because a refusal that names what exists is a disclosure of its own.

409.description: No link may be issued, and `code` is what distinguishes conditions whose remedies differ — branch on it, and treat a `code` you do not recognise as one more reason not to mint rather than as a transport fault. ⚠ The list below is what this route refuses today and nothing checks that it is complete; it went silently incomplete once already. `ENVELOPE_NOT_SENT` — the envelope has not been sent, so no recipient could have read it and none may be admitted to a ceremony over it. Send the envelope first; a token minted before the send would admit a recipient to a document the sender never released. `RECIPIENT_SLOT_NOT_CLAIMED` — the envelope is sent, but the recipient you named is a claimable slot nobody has claimed, so there is no party to admit. A signing token is a bearer credential: minted for a slot, whoever held it would become the party. Name somebody first with `POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/claim` — a claimed slot is an ordinary recipient and mints exactly like one, from this same call. `RECIPIENT_SIGNS_ELSEWHERE` — the recipient you named is declared to sign via `MACHINE_KEY`, so they never open a link and a signing token answers no need of theirs. There is no remedy on this route: the act is performed on their behalf over the machine surface. `RECIPIENT_STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` — the recipient you named sits on a step the workflow has not reached yet, so they may not act and must not hold a link that lets them. Mint again once their step has activated; nothing on this route tells you when that is. ⚠ NONE of them covers a terminal envelope: minting is refused only for an UNSENT one, so a link over a closed envelope is still issued here. What that link then buys is decided at `POST /signing/session`, not here — branch on ITS answer. ⛑ And a COMPLETED envelope is not a closed one for this purpose: its link opens, because a signer keeps the copy they signed (ADR-0059).

post.summary: Send this recipient their one-time code (machine twin of POST /signing/session/auth/otp/send)
post.description:
The platform mints and sends the code; the person reads it on their own device and gives it back to you, and you relay it to `POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/auth`.

⛔ This is not delegated signature. The recipient authenticates for real, with the method the sender declared; you carried the interaction, not the proof.

Rate limited on three counters. Two of them — this session and this destination — are the same ceilings a browser-driven send meets, because they protect the person. The third is keyed on your API client rather than on your server address, so one busy integration cannot exhaust another's budget.

200.description: A code is on its way, or one already live was reused.

409.description: Nothing was sent and nothing was charged. `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` — the workflow has not reached this recipient's step yet, so no session is opened and no code exists; call again once their step has activated. ⚠ Not the only 409 this route answers: it runs the same issuance as `POST /api/v1/signing/session/auth/otp/send`, whose 409 lists the other codes. Branch on `code`. ⚑ Two of those are the ceremony's lifecycle refusals and each names itself — `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` for an envelope that has ended, `LEG_CLOSED` for a recipient whose part is over on an envelope still open, each the same before and after the session is closed — so calling again cannot help: stop. Both are also the answer from the moment this recipient's step reaches its deadline without their act, before the scheduled sweep records it: `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` where that deadline ends the envelope, `LEG_CLOSED` where the envelope goes on. `LEG_CLOSED` is also what a recipient released before any session was opened for them gets: the leg is asked before this route opens the session, so it opens none and answers no not-found. A session already over (signed, declined or closed) answers the 401 `AUTH_NO_OPEN_CHALLENGE`; `SESSION_ALREADY_COMPLETED`, `SESSION_ALREADY_DECLINED` and `SESSION_CLOSED` reach this route only when the session closes between two reads of one request, and mean the same: stop.

429.description: Refused by the minimum interval between sends, or by one of the three ceilings. `Retry-After` says when. ⚠ A refusal on the session or destination counter is about this recipient; one on the client counter is about your integration as a whole.

post.summary: Relay this recipient's one-time code (machine twin of POST /signing/session/auth)
post.description:
You send us the code the recipient read on their own device. We verify it against the challenge we issued — the same budget, the same lockout, the same expiry a browser-driven answer meets.

On a passed ACCESS gate this returns the recipient's own session credential, which is what the following steps need. ⛔ That is the opposite of the delegated signature route, which mints nothing because its act opens and closes in one call.

200.description: The gate passed. An ACCESS gate also returns the credential pair.

401.description: The code was wrong, or the session is locked out. `code` distinguishes them and `Retry-After` is present on a soft lock.

409.description: `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` — the workflow has not reached this recipient's step yet, so the code is not checked and no attempt is spent; relay it again once their step has activated. ⚠ Not the only 409 this route answers: it runs the same verification as `POST /api/v1/signing/session/auth`, whose 409 lists the others. Branch on `code`. ⚑ Two of those are the ceremony's lifecycle refusals and each names itself — `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` for an envelope that has ended, `LEG_CLOSED` for a recipient whose part is over on an envelope still open, each the same before and after the session is closed; `LEG_CLOSED` also answers a right code whose recipient's part closed in the instant before the pass was recorded, which mints nothing and leaves the pass spent — so relaying the code again cannot help: stop. Both are also the answer from the moment this recipient's step reaches its deadline without their act, before the scheduled sweep records it: `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` where that deadline ends the envelope, `LEG_CLOSED` where the envelope goes on. A session already over (signed, declined or closed) answers the 401 `AUTH_NO_OPEN_CHALLENGE`; `SESSION_ALREADY_COMPLETED`, `SESSION_ALREADY_DECLINED` and `SESSION_CLOSED` reach this route only when the session closes between two reads of one request, and mean the same: stop.

post.summary: Commit a signature performed for a recipient inside the integrator's own system
post.description:
For a recipient the sender declared `signs_via: MACHINE_KEY`. The integrator authenticated the signatory itself and performed the act there; this records it. 

The act opens and closes in this one call: no session credential is minted, because there is nobody to hand one to. Everything downstream of the commit — the consent fact, the PAdES artifacts, the step advance — is identical to an ordinary ceremony.

`asserted_document_hashes` must cover exactly the documents this recipient signs. Fewer, more, or a digest that differs from the one held here is refused naming the document — re-read the documents and assert again.

asserted_subject.description: Your own opaque reference to the person who signed. ⛔ Not the `F5Sign-Declared-Subject` header, which names whoever made this call: this names who performed the signature, and only this becomes evidence.

asserted_consented_at.description: When that person performed the affirmative act, RFC 3339. It is per document rather than a standing authorisation: a framework agreement signed years ago is not consent to this.

asserted_document_hashes.description: Digest of each document, keyed by document id, as your system presented it. Must cover exactly what this recipient signs.

asserted_signer_ip.description: What your system observed of the person, if anything. Recorded as YOUR observation and never merged with ours.

asserted_auth_method.description: How your system authenticated them, in your own vocabulary. Recorded verbatim and not validated against ours.

reservations.description: Optional attest-with-exception note; the act still completes. The one place the text travels: a RESERVATIONS field only says where it is drawn, and its `max_length`, when authored, bounds this text.

filled_fields.description: What the recipient answered in your form, as you assert it — judged by the same rules as on the recipient's own route. ⚠ NEW, AND A CONTRACT CHANGE: if this recipient's envelope carries REQUIRED data fields, an act that sends none is now refused with FIELD_VALUES_INVALID naming them. ⛔ ABSENT IS NOT []: omit it only when you collected no form, and nothing is recorded; send it — even as [] — whenever you did, and every field shown to this recipient is recorded, a missing answer as a blank and a missing CHECKBOX as false. Only TEXT, DATE, CHECKBOX, DROPDOWN and RADIO fields of this recipient on documents they may read, for a SIGNER or APPROVER; any other entry is UNKNOWN_FIELD.

204.description: The act is recorded and the envelope has advanced.

409.description: The act may not be committed, and `code` distinguishes the conditions — branch on it. `ASSERTION_REQUIRED` — this recipient is declared to sign by machine key, so the act must carry the assertion describing it. `ASSERTION_NOT_ACCEPTED` — this recipient signs through our own ceremony, so the act must NOT carry an assertion: pass the gate over `POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/auth` first, then commit without asserting. `ENVELOPE_NOT_SENT` — the envelope has not been sent, so no ceremony exists over it yet. Send it first. `RECIPIENT_SLOT_NOT_CLAIMED` — the recipient is a claimable slot nobody has claimed, so there is no party to act for. Name somebody first. `SESSION_ALREADY_COMPLETED` — this recipient's leg is already finished; the repeat is refused and the first act stands. `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` — the envelope no longer accepts acts at the moment of the commit: it ended (a sender's void or close, another recipient's blocking decline or veto, its expiry date, or an ending no party decided), including when a step deadline that has passed, and is not yet processed, ends it. Every act on an ended envelope gets this answer, whether or not the session has been closed yet. Nothing was signed and nothing will be. `SESSION_CLOSED` — the session was closed without this recipient acting while the envelope and their part in it are both still open. A closed envelope or a released part never answers this: they answer `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` and `LEG_CLOSED`, before and after the session is closed. Not produced today; kept for a future cause. Nothing was signed; do not retry. `SIGNING_CHALLENGE_MISBOUND` — for a RELAYED act only: the signing code you relayed authorises a different set of documents than this act. Obtain a fresh code and relay that; re-sending the same one cannot succeed. ⛔ **Obtaining one takes `resend: true`** on `POST /api/v1/envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/auth/otp/send`: this refusal leaves the misbound challenge live and unspent, so the default `resend: false` finds it and answers `minted: false` with the same unusable code. The fresh one is bound to this act's documents at mint time; you send nothing about the documents. `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` — the workflow has not reached this recipient's step yet, so they may not act out of turn. ⛔ **The only one here that lifts by itself**: the act is well-formed and nothing is wrong with your call, so retry it once the step opens rather than changing what you send. `LEG_CLOSED` — the envelope is still open, but this recipient's part in it is already over, as the envelope judges it at the moment of the act: an act of theirs was already admitted, or their leg was released without one (their step closed without them while the envelope went on), including when their step's deadline has passed, is not yet processed, and the envelope goes on without them. (A closed envelope answers `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` instead, ahead of this.) The same answer before and after the session itself is closed. Nothing was signed by this call and nothing reopens the leg: do not retry, and do not wait for it to lift as you would for `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE`. `COMMIT_NOT_OFFERED_TO_ROLE` — this recipient's role is read-only (VIEWER, REVIEWER, EDITOR): it never commits and never holds its step, so the workflow does not wait for it. Nothing was signed and the same act never succeeds: do not commit for these roles. ⚑ **And one condition here carries the bare `CONFLICT` deliberately**: a relayed `SIGNING_PLATFORM` recipient whose access gate has not been passed. Relay the code over `POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/auth` first, then commit. ⚠ These are conflicts rather than not-founds because you are the sender: an id you supplied is one you already know exists.

422.description: The act does not describe what it must — branch on `code`. `ASSERTED_DOCUMENT_MISMATCH` — a digest differs from the one held here, a document you must assert is missing, or you named one this recipient does not sign. `detail` names the document. Re-read it and assert again. `FIELD_VALUES_INVALID` — the asserted answers broke their fields' rules; `field_errors` names every bad field at once (see FieldValueError) and nothing was recorded. It never answers ahead of a refusal of the act itself (already completed, no longer live, `LEG_CLOSED`, `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE`, closed): the act is admitted first and its values judged inside that admission. `VALIDATION_ERROR` — the body is malformed; `errors[]` names the member.

get.summary: Read the signing session read-model for the recipient credential

200.description: The recipient read-model (envelope, documents, fields, signer).

401.description: The credential is missing, malformed, expired — or RETIRED. ⚑ Discriminate on `code`: `CREDENTIAL_RETIRED` means a sender gesture (a corrected contact, or a reset access code) has since superseded the credential you hold. ⛔ It is RECOVERABLE and a bare 401 is not: send the signer back through their invitation link to pass the gate again — with the new access code if the sender reset one — rather than to a dead-end error screen. ⚠ The response never says WHICH gesture fired: a wrongly-addressed invitation must not learn that its address was corrected.

409.description: There is no ceremony to read, for one of two unrelated reasons — discriminate on the `code` member, never on the status. (a) The recipient has no interactive ceremony to read RIGHT NOW: `RECIPIENT_DELEGATED`, `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE`, `ROLE_NOT_INTERACTIVE`, or `LEG_CLOSED` — this recipient's part is over while the envelope is still open, released without acting (a step's deadline), answered at once on a credential minted before it closed; a released member who reads as informational is not refused. ⚑ **`STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` is the one of the four that can change on its own**: it means the workflow has not reached this recipient's step yet (or the step was skipped). Their credential stays valid and their turn may still arrive, so show "not your turn yet" rather than an error, and do not send them back through their link — the other three are settled for this recipient and will not lift. (b) `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` — the envelope no longer hands its document to recipients and the leg closed underneath this recipient. ⛔ Branch on this `code`, never on a list of envelope states: which states produce it is ours to change and is not published here, precisely so a list copied into your code cannot go stale without anything failing. ⚑ What IS a promise: a signed envelope does NOT produce it — it keeps serving this route and the document bytes, so the signer can still fetch the copy they signed. Nor does an envelope that ended without agreement, for a recipient who signed in it or who reads as informational: they are served its sealed record once it lands. A recipient who declined, or was released without having acted, meets this code instead (ADR-0073 §2.15, narrowing ADR-0070 §2.6) — a refusal is proven by the evidence document, not by a PDF carrying others' signatures. This one is published rather than hidden precisely because the recipient DID legitimately have a ceremony: show them that their part in it is over, rather than the broken-link screen a 404 would earn — and not that the document was cancelled, because an envelope also closes agreed without them; `outcome` and `envelope_outcome` on `GET /api/v1/signing/session/auth` say how it ended. Their credential is still valid and still buys nothing — do not re-authenticate, and do not retry. (c) `SEAL_PENDING` — the envelope closed and this recipient signed in it, or reads as informational, so they are entitled to its sealed record, which is being sealed after the fact. ⚑ **It lifts by itself**: the same read answers 200 once the seal lands. Say the record is being prepared, not that anything failed.

post.summary: Open or resume the signing session for the bearer token

200.description: `status` is the state of the SESSION, not of what the sender declared: `AUTH_PASSED` means the access gate is behind this recipient and the leg is still open, `AUTH_PENDING` that a declared gate is still unmet — route those to `POST /api/v1/signing/session/auth`. `COMPLETED` means this recipient has signed: route it to your done screen and NEVER to the auth screen, because nothing further can be asked and every send attempt will refuse with `AUTH_NO_OPEN_CHALLENGE` (ADR-0053 §2.3 row 1). ⚠ `AUTH_PASSED` does NOT imply a credential is in this body. Re-opening the link never mints behind a declared gate; passing the gate is the only thing that does. So a recipient who passed the gate on an EARLIER request and has since lost the pair — a mobile tab discarded while they read their code — is answered `AUTH_PASSED` with the three credential members ABSENT (not null) and `access_grant_expires_at` saying when the grant they can no longer use lapses. ⛔ Branch on the PRESENCE of `access_credential`, never on `status` alone.

status.description: The SESSION's own state, and never a fact about the declaration. COMPLETED once this recipient has signed — terminal, and it takes precedence over the other two, which is the whole of ADR-0056: a signed session HAS passed the access gate, so it read AUTH_PASSED until 2026-08-24 and clients routed it back into the ceremony. AUTH_PASSED once the access gate has been passed and the leg is still open — including the neutral gate, where arriving with the link IS passing it. AUTH_PENDING while a declared gate is unmet, which covers both a gate never passed and a grant withdrawn after going idle. ⛔ COMPLETED does NOT imply this body withholds a credential: a terminal session whose access gate is neutral still mints one, and that recipient can read the read-model and download their sealed copy. ⚠ Says nothing about whether this body carries a credential — branch on presence for that. REVOKED means the envelope closed this recipient's part underneath a live session without their act — it ended without agreement, or released them — and that they may not read on. ⛑ **Both are terminal, and what separates them is what the recipient still has behind each.** Behind COMPLETED there is something of theirs to collect — the copy they signed, for as long as their link lives (ADR-0059). Behind REVOKED there is nothing: their part is over with nothing of theirs in it, and no gate, code or credential produces anything on the other side. ⚑ That is a fact about the contract and not about your UI, but the asymmetry your routing needs follows from it: a client enters a ceremony to collect something, so where there is nothing to collect, entering buys nothing — which is why REVOKED does not belong nested under whatever branch you use for a credential pair. ⚑ Today you will not see REVOKED here: a session is revoked only for a recipient whose gate is shut — a member who may still read after the close (an informational member, or one who signed) keeps theirs (2026-09-29) — and a shut gate is refused with 409 before this body is built. It is published anyway: that coupling lives in another decision and is not this route's to promise, and an enum missing a value its own source can return is how a client ends up in its 'unknown status' branch on the day the coupling moves. DECLINED means this recipient declined their leg (ADR-0070): terminal, their own act, and not a signature — show their declined state, never the ceremony.

access_credential.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer` on the read-model, document and commit routes. Fifteen minutes. ABSENT — not null — whenever this response mints nothing, which is every open behind a declared gate, `AUTH_PASSED` ones included.

refresh_credential.description: Shown once. Store it alongside the access credential — renewal needs BOTH, so a client that keeps only this one cannot renew. Absent on the same responses as `access_credential`.

expires_at.description: When the access credential in THIS body expires — fifteen minutes. Absent on the same responses as `access_credential`. ⚠ Not `access_grant_expires_at`, which is the hour-long grant behind it.

access_grant_expires_at.description: When the access grant stops being renewable — the idle deadline (ADR-0050 §2.5), an hour from the last mint or renewal. NULL, never absent, when the session holds no grant: none has been minted, or one was withdrawn. ⛔ Not a retry time and not `expires_at`. It is when the CURRENT grant lapses, so a recipient stranded on `AUTH_PASSED` without a credential regains the door once it passes — but a second live tab that keeps renewing pushes it forward, so re-read it rather than counting down from a cached value. ⛔ **That recovery does NOT apply to `COMPLETED`, and the instant published there is already in the past and always will be.** A terminal session is never withdrawn as idle, so it never re-opens its gate: this member keeps reporting the deadline of the grant the signer held when they signed. Read `status` FIRST — a countdown drawn from this value on a signed session is a promise nothing can keep.

409.description: No session is opened and this call mints NOTHING: no session credential, no refresh credential. `code` distinguishes four conditions with different remedies — branch on it. `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` — this envelope has closed and no longer hands its document to this recipient, so their ceremony is over. ⛔ This is a terminal answer for the link, not a transient failure: do NOT retry. A client that treats a non-2xx here as a transport fault will retry forever. ⚠ It does NOT mean the document was cancelled: an envelope also closes agreed without this recipient's part (the sender closed it once agreement was secured, or a deadline passed). To say how it ended, read `outcome` (what happened to this participation) and `envelope_outcome` (`AGREED` or `NOT_AGREED`) on `GET /api/v1/signing/session/auth`, which this same link still reaches. ⚑ It is also the answer from the moment this recipient's step reaches its deadline, when that deadline ends the envelope and this recipient had not signed: the scheduled sweep records the close up to a minute later, and the answer does not wait for it. `LEG_CLOSED` — this recipient's part is over while the envelope is still open (they declined, or their leg closed without their signature): the link opens nothing more for them. Terminal for the link, like the one above; do NOT retry. It is also the answer from the moment this recipient's step reaches its deadline without their signature while the envelope goes on, before the scheduled sweep has recorded the release. ⚑ It is decided twice, the second time under a lock as the opening is recorded, so a leg closed in the instant between the two (a step deadline releasing this recipient) is refused with this same code rather than handed a credential. `RECIPIENT_SIGNS_ELSEWHERE` — the sender declared this recipient to sign through an integrator, so this link opens nothing, now or later. `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` — the workflow has not reached this recipient's step yet: the ceremony is theirs but has not begun. Tell the signer it is not their turn yet; the same link opens once their step is active. ⚠ None of these is a member of `status`: that field reports the state of the SESSION, and on this path no session is opened at all.

get.summary: Which gate does this recipient face right now?
get.description: Answers before the code is typed, so it takes the emailed signing token rather than the session credential. Serves BOTH gates: while the access gate is unmet it describes that one; once it is passed it describes the signing gate, if the sender declared one. `gate` is null when nothing further is being asked — which is two states, separated by `outcome`: null means the recipient may proceed, non-null means the leg is closed and nothing can be asked ever again. ⚑ `access_gate` is separate and does NOT go null in either: it says what this recipient's door is, which is what a client needs to render the right control when recovering a lost session. Never carries a verifier, a code, or a count of remaining attempts.

200.description: What is being asked of this recipient right now.

gate.description: ACCESS while the door is unmet, SIGNING once it is passed and a signing gate is declared, null when nothing is being asked. ⚠ null is TWO states — read `outcome` to tell them apart.

outcome.description: HOW this recipient's leg closed, or null while it is still open. ⛔ Read it BEFORE `gate`: non-null means the ceremony is over and NO control should be rendered, whatever else this body carries. null covers both a live session and a session not yet opened — this route is callable before the first open — because neither is closed, which is the only question this member answers. ⚠ `access_gate` REMAINS populated on a closed leg, deliberately: it describes the door, which does not stop existing because the leg closed. Branching on `access_gate != null` to decide whether recovery is possible is the exact confusion this member exists to remove. ⚑ A nullable discriminator rather than a boolean so it grows: a terminal state that is not a completion names itself here instead of having to answer a `completed` flag, where both true and false are wrong. Treat a value you do not recognise as closed-but-unnameable: show something that neither affirms a signature nor offers the ceremony. ⚠ That is a PROPERTY, not a navigation instruction — this said `route to a neutral screen` until 2026-08-24, and the first client to implement it reported back that routing was the one thing it could not do there: its status screens demand a verdict for that link, an unknown outcome gives it nothing to prove one with, and navigating would have bounced back into the auth screen. It resolves in place instead, which satisfies every word of the property. ⛔ Do NOT invent an error code to make navigation possible; this route answers 200 and the branch is unreachable until the union grows. ⚑ **It grew on 2026-08-26 with REVOKED, and REVOKED narrowed on 2026-09-29**: it no longer says the envelope ended without agreement — read `envelope_outcome` for what happened to the envelope. It now means only that this recipient's leg was closed in a way this union has no other name for, and nothing in this system closes a leg that way today: treat it exactly as the closed-but-unnameable branch above — never a signed-successfully screen, never the auth control. ⛔ It is NOT an error and NOT a retry: the same link will keep answering 200 with this value. ⚑ **And again with TASK-046**: DECLINED means this recipient declined their leg (ADR-0070) — their own act, irreversible. Show their declined state; never a signed screen and never the auth control. ⚑ **And again with ADR-0073 (§2.9)**: RELEASED means the envelope closed while this recipient's part was still open, and released them — they did nothing, and nothing more is asked of them. It is published whether or not they ever opened a session, and whatever became of it: a session the release closed reads RELEASED too, never REVOKED. A step deadline releases a member who has not acted, whether the envelope then goes on or ends, and RELEASED is published from the deadline itself, before the scheduled sweep records the release up to a minute later. Show that their participation is over; never a signed screen and never the auth control — and read `envelope_outcome` to say whether the envelope was agreed without them or ended without agreement. A released member who may still read (an informational member, or anyone who signed) is let back in instead and never sees it: an informational member reads `outcome: null` beside a non-null `envelope_outcome`, which is the pair that means *the envelope is over and your copy is there to read*.

envelope_outcome.description: How the ENVELOPE ended — AGREED or NOT_AGREED — or null while it has not closed. A fact about the whole envelope, never about this recipient: `outcome` says what happened to THIS participation, this says what happened to the document. Read the two together. `outcome: RELEASED` with AGREED: the envelope was agreed without this recipient's part; with NOT_AGREED: it ended without agreement. `outcome: null` with a non-null value: the envelope is over and this recipient is let back in to read the final copy (an informational member). `outcome: COMPLETED`: this recipient signed, whichever way the envelope ended. ⚠ null while the envelope is open, even once enough signatures are in to guarantee agreement: the envelope has not ended until it closes. Set at the close, which can come before the sealed copy exists — reads wait for the seal, and say so by name. ⚑ One exception to the null, and it is the same answer early: once this recipient's step has passed a deadline that ends the envelope, the value it closes with is published from the deadline itself, before the scheduled sweep records the close up to a minute later.

method.description: The method IN FORCE for that gate right now; null when `gate` is null. That is the gate's first declared method until the signer chooses another, and the chosen one afterwards (ADR-0054 §2.6) — so it is what a code will actually be sent on, not merely what the sender listed first. `masked_destination` and `code_length` beside it follow THIS method. Read `methods` below for the whole declared list and to render a chooser. ⚠ Published as a bare string until 2026-08-19, which told a client nothing it could switch on — it is the same fifteen-member vocabulary `auth_requirements[].method` carries.

masked_destination.description: Where a delivered code will be sent for the gate named by `gate`, masked server-side and handed over already masked — do not reconstruct it client-side. Null for ACCESS_CODE, which is never delivered, and null when no address is on file. Served ONLY on this route: the re-send route carries no destination in any form.

access_gate.description: What this recipient's DOOR is, independently of what is being asked right now. `gate`/`method` answer the live question and go null once the access gate is behind the signer; this stays, so a client can render the right control when recovering a lost session (`recover: true`). NULL — never absent — when the access gate is neutral, which is also exactly when recovery is neither possible nor needed. ⚠ Do NOT branch your auth screen on this: it says what the door is, not that you are being asked for it. Read `gate` for that.

method.description: The method in force at the DOOR — same reading as `method` above, applied to the access gate whatever is being asked right now. Same fifteen-member vocabulary.

masked_destination.description: Where a recovery code would go, already masked. Null for a method that delivers nothing — eleven of the fifteen — and null when no address is on file.

code_length.description: Characters in the code for the DECLARED ACCESS method. Same meaning and same nulls as the top-level `code_length`.

methods.description: Every method the DOOR declares, in the sender's order, head included — the same shape and the same rules as the top-level `methods`. Render the recovery chooser from this one; the top-level list describes whatever gate is live, which after passage is the other one.

selection.description: How the DOOR's list is presented — same meaning and same values as the top-level `selection`, restated here so the recovery control never has to read its own mode off another block. Always present when `access_gate` is.

code_length.description: How many characters the code for `method` will have, so a segmented input can size itself instead of guessing. ⛔ NULL means NOT KNOWABLE, never "no code": a sender-supplied ACCESS_CODE reaches us only as a hash, so there is no length to report — render a single free-text field there, because the floor a sender must clear is not a width and the pattern it exists for (a national id) is longer and not numeric. Non-null exactly for the four delivered methods, whose codes we generate through one generator, so the width is uniform by construction. Also null when `gate` is null.

methods.description: EVERY method the gate named by `gate` declares, in the SENDER'S ORDER, with the method currently in force included rather than filtered out — so one row of the chooser is never composed from the flat fields above while the rest come from here. ⛔ A LIST, never a map keyed by method: the order is the declaration, and under the default escalation mode the first entry is the one that actually gets sent. Empty when `gate` is null; the key is always present. To move the signer onto another entry, POST its `method` to /signing/session/auth/otp/send — that MINTS (the live code stops working) and waits out the same cooldown as a re-send, so offer it from `next_resend_at` onwards.

selection.description: How this recipient's declared list is PRESENTED, which decides what your auth screen does on mount. `ESCALATION` — a code for `method` is already on its way (or will be the moment you call the send route with no body), and the other entries in `methods` become selectable from `next_resend_at`. `FREE_CHOICE` — NOTHING HAS BEEN SENT and nothing will be until the signer picks: render the chooser first, and until they do there is no code, no `code_expires_at` and no `next_resend_at`, so draw no clock. Calling the send route with no `method` under free choice is a 409 `AUTH_METHOD_NOT_CHOSEN`. ⚑ Published per gate block, and both blocks carry the same value today because the mode is a property of the RECIPIENT — read each block's own rather than the other's, so a recovery control never depends on which gate happens to be live, and so a per-gate mode later needs no shape change. Changing method during the cooldown stays allowed either way: the cooldown belongs to the gate, not to the method.

document_title.description: What the signer is unlocking. Present so the auth screen is not an anonymous code box (ADR-0049 §2.3, amended 2026-08-18).

locale.description: The recipient's declared language, or null when nobody stated one — fall through to your own default rather than reading a choice off the absence.

409.description: Nothing is described: no gate, no method, no destination, no title. The only `code` this route answers 409 with today is `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` — the workflow has not reached this recipient's step yet, so the ceremony is theirs but has not begun. Tell the signer it is not their turn yet and render no auth control; the same link is described normally once their step is active. Branch on `code` rather than on the status, because a later refusal here would share it.

post.summary: Answer the gate this recipient currently faces
post.description: Verifies the submitted code against whichever gate is open — the access gate while the door is shut, the signing gate once it is not. Passing the ACCESS gate returns the session credential pair, and is the ONLY way one is minted behind a declared gate: re-opening the link does not. Passing the SIGNING gate returns no credential, because it grants nothing durable — its proof is consumed by the commit. A wrong code is never free: it spends the attempt budget even though the request fails, so a client must not retry automatically.

access_credential.description: Present only when `gate_passed` is ACCESS. Send as `Authorization: Bearer` on the read-model, document and commit routes.

refresh_credential.description: Present only when `gate_passed` is ACCESS. Shown once; renewal needs BOTH halves.

401.description: The code was wrong, the challenge had expired, nothing was open, or the session went idle and the access gate must be repeated. Distinguish on the problem `code`: AUTH_CODE_INCORRECT, AUTH_CHALLENGE_EXPIRED, AUTH_NO_OPEN_CHALLENGE, AUTH_REAUTH_REQUIRED, AUTH_GATE_MISCONFIGURED. ⚑ `recover: true` is IGNORED for a recipient whose access gate is NEUTRAL — the route answers exactly as it would without it (the signing gate if one is declared, otherwise AUTH_NO_OPEN_CHALLENGE). There is no door to re-pass, and none is needed: re-opening the link mints a fresh pair for those recipients, so they are never stranded.

409.description: `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` — the workflow has not reached this recipient's step yet, so the code is not checked and no attempt is spent; tell the signer it is not their turn yet. The ceremony's lifecycle refusals reach this route too, and each names itself: `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` — the envelope has ended and this recipient may no longer pass its gate; `LEG_CLOSED` — the envelope is still open but this recipient's part in it is over (their leg was released without an act of theirs). Each is the same answer before and after the session is closed, the code is not checked and no attempt is spent. Both are also the answer from the moment this recipient's step reaches its deadline without their act, before the scheduled sweep records it: `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` where that deadline ends the envelope, `LEG_CLOSED` where the envelope goes on. `LEG_CLOSED` has one more occasion: the code was right, but this recipient's part closed without their signature (a step deadline released them) in the instant before the pass was recorded, so no credential is minted and the pass stays spent. Neither lifts by itself: stop, and do not re-prompt for a code. ⚑ A session that is already over — the recipient signed or declined, or it was closed while the envelope and their part are still open — is answered by the 401 `AUTH_NO_OPEN_CHALLENGE`, not here. `SESSION_ALREADY_COMPLETED`, `SESSION_ALREADY_DECLINED` and `SESSION_CLOSED` reach this route only when the session closes between two reads of one request, and mean the same: stop.

423.description: Hard lock (`AUTH_HARD_LOCKED`). No amount of waiting lifts this — the sender must reset the access code. Do NOT retry.

429.description: Soft lock (`AUTH_COOLING_DOWN`). Releases itself; `Retry-After` carries the wait in seconds and is exposed cross-origin. Distinct from 423 on purpose: this one says wait, that one says call the sender.

post.summary: Issue or re-send the one-time code for the gate this recipient faces
post.description: Serves BOTH of the two issuance operations, discriminated by `resend`. With `resend: false` (the default, and what the auth screen should call on mount) a code that is already live is left alone and NOTHING is sent — read `minted` to find out which happened, and do not tell the signer a message was sent when it was false. With `resend: true` (the re-send control) a new code is minted and THE CODE ALREADY IN THE INBOX STOPS WORKING — so do not wire component-mount to it, or a page reload will kill the code the signer is reading. Which gate is being answered is decided server-side and there is still no gate field. ⚑ There IS an optional `method` field since ADR-0054: omit it and nothing changes, send it and the signer moves to that member of the gate's declared list — which MINTS, obeys the same cooldown, and is refused with 409 if the gate does not declare it. The response never names the destination in any form: the masked address is served once, by GET /signing/session/auth.

200.description: A live code exists for this gate.

minted.description: Whether this call actually sent a message. `false` means a live code was already outstanding and was returned untouched — say "enter the code we sent you", not "sent". Only `resend: false` can return `false`.

code_expires_at.description: When the live code stops being accepted. 15 minutes for OTP_EMAIL.

next_resend_at.description: First instant a `resend: true` call will not be refused. MAY BE IN THE PAST, meaning a re-send is allowed now — draw no countdown in that case. Not clamped, deliberately.

401.description: Nothing is being asked of this recipient, so there is no code to send (`AUTH_NO_OPEN_CHALLENGE`). A caller that already passed every gate and sent `recover: false` lands here; `recover: true` is what asks for the access gate again. A session that is already over also lands here, and `recover: true` does not change that: the recipient signed or declined, or the session was closed while the envelope and their part are still open. A closed envelope or a released part answers the 409 instead (`ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE`, `LEG_CLOSED`).

404.description: The link names nothing this recipient can reach, or no session has been opened for it yet: `POST /api/v1/signing/session` opens it, and this route never does. ⚑ Not for a recipient whose part is already over: one released before they ever opened the link has no session either, and is answered by the 409 `LEG_CLOSED`, because the leg is asked before the session is looked up.

409.description: Nothing can be sent for this gate, or not the thing you asked for. `AUTH_METHOD_NOT_DECLARED` — you sent a `method` this recipient's gate does not declare. It is NEVER silently replaced by the first declared method: a request meaning "send me an SMS" must not be answered with an email under a 200. Re-read the declared list from GET /api/v1/signing/session/auth, which is the only place it is published. `AUTH_METHOD_NOT_DELIVERED` — the gate is an ACCESS_CODE one, whose secret the sender shared out of band; the recovery of the CODE is the sender resetting it, never this route. ⚑ That is unrelated to `recover: true`, which recovers a lost SESSION and needs no call here at all for an ACCESS_CODE gate — send the code straight to `POST /api/v1/signing/session/auth` with `recover: true`. `AUTH_NO_DESTINATION` — no address is on file. `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` — the workflow has not reached this recipient's step yet, so no code is sent and nothing is charged; tell the signer it is not their turn yet. Also the lifecycle refusals, each naming itself: `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` — the envelope has ended and this recipient may no longer pass its gate; `LEG_CLOSED` — the envelope is still open but this recipient's part in it is over (their leg was released without an act of theirs), including a recipient released before they ever opened the link, who has no session and is answered here, not with the 404. Each is the same answer before and after the session is closed. Both are also the answer from the moment this recipient's step reaches its deadline without their act, before the scheduled sweep records it: `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` where that deadline ends the envelope, `LEG_CLOSED` where the envelope goes on. Nothing is sent and nothing is charged for either, and neither lifts by itself. ⚑ A session that is already over — the recipient signed or declined, or it was closed while the envelope and their part are still open — is answered by the 401 `AUTH_NO_OPEN_CHALLENGE`, not here. `SESSION_ALREADY_COMPLETED`, `SESSION_ALREADY_DECLINED` and `SESSION_CLOSED` reach this route only when the session closes between two reads of one request, and mean the same: stop.

423.description: Hard lock (`AUTH_HARD_LOCKED`) — no amount of waiting lifts this. Do NOT retry.

429.description: Refused for now (`OTP_SEND_COOLING_DOWN`). One code covers all four ways this route refuses — the 60-second minimum interval and each of the three limiter keys — because two of those keys refuse people who did nothing wrong. ⚑ CHOOSING A METHOD LANDS HERE TOO, and that is the design rather than an accident: a selection is a mint, so it waits out the same interval a re-send does (ADR-0054 §2.8 — changing channel must not restart the clock, or the selector becomes a cooldown bypass). SURFACE IT AS A COUNTDOWN, NOT AN ERROR. The wait arrives three ways: the `Retry-After` header (exposed cross-origin), `retry_after_seconds` in the body, and `retry_at` as an absolute instant — prefer the last, because a relative countdown drifts while the signer is away reading their email.

get.summary: Download the latest available document bytes for the credential's recipient

200.description: The latest available document bytes (tip of the artifact chain).

404.description:
No bytes are served. One answer for every reason — an unknown document, one this recipient may not see, one with nothing uploaded yet, an envelope that was never sent, one that no longer hands its document to recipients (never merely because it COMPLETED — a signer keeps their signed copy, ADR-0059 — nor, once sealed, one that ended without agreement to a recipient who signed in it or reads as informational; a recipient who declined, or was released without acting, is refused here instead (ADR-0073 §2.15, narrowing ADR-0070 §2.6)), an envelope that ended without agreement whose sealed record is not ready yet, one whose credential a sender gesture has retired (ADR-0060), one whose recipient sits on a step the workflow has not reached yet (ADR-0066), and one whose recipient's part is over while the envelope is still open — released without acting (a step's deadline), or declined — unless they signed or read as informational (ADR-0073 §2.3): refused at once, whatever credential they still hold. ⚠ The reasons are deliberately indistinguishable HERE: telling them apart would disclose what an envelope contains to someone with no right to it. `GET /api/v1/signing/session` is the surface that explains them: it answers 409 `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` for a closed envelope, 401 `CREDENTIAL_RETIRED` for a superseded credential, 409 `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` for a turn that has not arrived, 409 `SEAL_PENDING` for a sealed record still being prepared, 409 `LEG_CLOSED` for a part released without acting, and 200 with `status: DECLINED` for a recipient who declined. Read it before rendering an error — they need different screens, and not all of them are recoverable. 

⛑ **GUARANTEE — the two routes cannot disagree about your entitlement.** If you answer this 404 by re-asking `GET /api/v1/signing/session` and it replies **200**, then the 404 was NOT about the envelope being closed, NOT about your credential and NOT about your turn not having arrived: both routes answer those three questions from one read of the same recipient context, so a 200 there rules them out. ⚠ Except a 200 whose `status` is `DECLINED`: that recipient's part is over, and this route serves them nothing — show their declined state, never a retry. Otherwise, what is left is a document reason — unknown, not yours, or nothing uploaded yet — and only the last of those is worth a retry control. ⚑ You may rely on this: it is held by `SigningReadersCannotDisagreeTest`, which drives both readers off one context for every envelope status and for the credential, never-sent and step axes. 

⛑ **GUARANTEE — a 200 carries the whole document.** The artifact is fully in hand before this endpoint answers; there is no path where a 200 precedes it being materialized.
