So a short or empty body is a TRANSPORT failure, never a partially ready document, and the right response is to fail loudly rather than to save what arrived — a zero-byte file in the signer's downloads folder is the worst possible outcome, because that file is the copy they keep as proof.

post.summary: Commit the recipient signature on the session

consent.description: Explicit signing consent — must be true.

reservations.description: Optional attest-with-exception note (eCMR "recibí con incidencias"); the signature still completes. The ONE place the text travels: a RESERVATIONS field only says where it is drawn, and its `max_length`, when authored, bounds this text (a longer one is refused with a `TOO_LONG` record on that field).

filled_fields.description: What the recipient answered in the form they were shown — the final values, recorded once, with this commit. ⛔ ABSENT IS NOT []: omit the member only when this client showed no form; nothing is then recorded, not even a blank, though a REQUIRED field is still owed and refused. Send it — even as [] — whenever the form was shown: every field you were shown is then recorded, a missing or null/"" answer as a blank and a missing CHECKBOX as unticked (false). Only fields of type TEXT, DATE, CHECKBOX, DROPDOWN and RADIO from this session's `fields`, never readonly ones, and only when the recipient's role is SIGNER or APPROVER: any other entry — blank ones included — is refused as UNKNOWN_FIELD. RESERVATIONS text goes in `reservations`, never here.

401.description: The credential is missing, malformed, expired — or RETIRED. ⚑ Discriminate on `code`: `CREDENTIAL_RETIRED` means a sender gesture (a corrected contact, or a reset access code) has since superseded the credential you hold. ⛔ It is RECOVERABLE and a bare 401 is not: send the signer back through their invitation link to pass the gate again — with the new access code if the sender reset one — rather than to a dead-end error screen. ⚠ The response never says WHICH gesture fired: a wrongly-addressed invitation must not learn that its address was corrected.

404.description: No session has been opened for this token yet. A freshly minted token is in this state until `POST /signing/session` runs, which is the only session producer — so committing first is a reachable client ordering, not a malformed request.

409.description: The act may not be committed. **Branch on `code`, and treat a `code` you do not recognise as *stop, and do not retry as-is*** — the safe reading, and what each code below means unless it says otherwise. `SESSION_ALREADY_COMPLETED` — this leg is finished by this recipient's own act, so a second commit on the same still-valid credential lands here rather than signing twice. ⛑ **This one is a success arriving late**: show the signed state, not a failure. `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` — the envelope no longer accepts acts at the moment of the commit: it ended (a sender's void or close, another recipient's blocking decline or veto, its expiry date, or an ending no party decided), including when a step deadline that has passed, and is not yet processed, ends it. Every act on an ended envelope gets this answer, whether or not the signing session has been closed yet. **Nothing was signed and nothing will be**; do not retry, and do not show a completed state. The credential stays valid and buys nothing, which is a refusal and not a revocation. `SESSION_CLOSED` — the signing session was closed without this recipient acting while the envelope and their part in it are both still open. A closed envelope or a released part never answers this: they answer `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` and `LEG_CLOSED`, before and after the session is closed. Not produced today; kept for a future cause. **Nothing was signed**; do not retry, and do not show a completed state. `SIGNING_CHALLENGE_MISBOUND` — the signing code this signer answered authorises a different set of documents than this act. **Re-read the documents and obtain a FRESH signing code**; do not re-submit this act and do not re-prompt for the same code, which cannot succeed. ⛔ **Asking for one is not enough: send `POST /api/v1/signing/session/auth/otp/send` with `resend: true`.** This refusal leaves the misbound challenge live, verified and unspent — it is checked and not consumed — so the default `resend: false` means *ensure a code exists*, finds that one and answers `minted: false` with it, which is the loop the sentence above forbids. A forced one is bound to THIS act's documents when it is minted, so nothing about the documents travels in that request. ⚑ Unlike this one, an EXPIRED challenge stops being live on its own, so `AUTH_CHALLENGE_EXPIRED` needs no forcing: ensuring already mints. `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` — the workflow has not reached this recipient's step yet, so they may not sign out of turn. ⛔ **This is the one that lifts by itself.** The credential stays valid and the same commit succeeds once their step opens: show "not your turn yet" rather than a signing failure, and do not send the signer back through their link. `LEG_CLOSED` — the envelope is still open, but this recipient's part in it is already over, as the envelope judges it at the moment of the act: an act of theirs was already admitted, or their leg was released without one (their step closed without them while the envelope went on), including when their step's deadline has passed, is not yet processed, and the envelope goes on without them. (A closed envelope answers `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` instead, ahead of this.) The same answer before and after the signing session itself is closed. **Nothing was signed by this call, and nothing the workflow does later reopens the leg**: do not retry, and do not show "not your turn yet" — unlike `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE`, this one never lifts. `COMMIT_NOT_OFFERED_TO_ROLE` — this recipient's role is read-only (VIEWER, REVIEWER, EDITOR): it never commits and never holds its step, so the workflow does not wait for it. **Nothing was signed, and the same commit never succeeds**: do not offer a signing action to these roles, and show the documents to read instead. ⚠ Nothing checks that this description is complete, so read it as what the route refuses today rather than as a closed set.

422.description: Two different refusals — branch on `code`. `FIELD_VALUES_INVALID` — the answers broke their fields' rules, and `field_errors` names EVERY bad field at once, one code each (see FieldValueError). Nothing was recorded and nothing was spent: correct the form and commit again with the SAME signing code, which a refused commit never consumes. `VALIDATION_ERROR` — the body itself is malformed (`errors[]` names the member): consent not true, a `filled_fields` that is not a list of { field_id, value }, a number as a value, a field answered twice. A client defect.

post.summary: Decline the recipient's leg on the session

reason.description: Why the recipient declines, in their own words. Required and not blank, at most 500 characters, and no control characters other than tab, line feed and carriage return. The sender reads it on the envelope; it is never written into the document. ⛔ Send only this member: the session is named by the credential, so there is no `session_id` in the body.

200.description: Declined; the session is closed as DECLINED. ⛔ Irreversible. When the recipient is blocking (SIGNER, APPROVER) the envelope then closes without agreement, `outcome: NOT_AGREED` with `end_cause: RECIPIENT_DECLINED` — read the envelope for that, it is not in this response.

401.description: The credential is missing, malformed, expired — or it no longer admits this act. Discriminate on `code`. `CREDENTIAL_RETIRED` — a sender gesture superseded the credential: send the signer back through their invitation link. `AUTH_REAUTH_REQUIRED` — the access grant went idle: pass the access gate again, then decline. A closed envelope or a released part answers the 409 first (`ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE`, `LEG_CLOSED`), so an idle grant is never sent to re-authenticate for nothing. Renewing the credential fixes neither.

404.description: No session has been opened for this credential's scope.

409.description: The decline may not be made. **Branch on `code`**; a code you do not recognise means stop, and do not retry as-is. `SESSION_ALREADY_DECLINED` — this recipient already declined; show their declined state. `SESSION_ALREADY_COMPLETED` — this recipient already signed; a signature is not undone by a later refusal. `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` — the envelope had already ended when the decline arrived (a sender's void or close, another recipient's blocking decline or veto, its expiry date, or an ending no party decided), including when a step deadline that has passed, and is not yet processed, ends it. Every act on an ended envelope gets this answer, whether or not the session has been closed yet. Nothing was declined; do not retry. `SESSION_CLOSED` — the session was closed without this recipient acting while the envelope and their part in it are both still open. A closed envelope or a released part never answers this: they answer `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` and `LEG_CLOSED`, before and after the session is closed. Not produced today; kept for a future cause. `STEP_NOT_ACTIVE` — the workflow has not reached this recipient yet; the same decline succeeds once their step opens. `LEG_CLOSED` — the envelope is still open, but this recipient's part in it is already over, as the envelope judges it at the moment of the decline: an act of theirs was already admitted, or their leg was released without one (their step closed without them while the envelope went on), including when their step's deadline has passed, is not yet processed, and the envelope goes on without them. (A closed envelope answers `ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE` instead, ahead of this.) The same answer before and after the session itself is closed. Nothing was declined and nothing reopens the leg; do not retry. `DECLINE_NOT_OFFERED_TO_ROLE` — this recipient's role may not decline (only SIGNER, APPROVER and CERTIFIED_DELIVERY may); hide the action.

422.description: `VALIDATION_ERROR` — the body is malformed: `reason` missing, blank, longer than 500 characters, or carrying a control character (`errors[]` names the member). Nothing was declined.

post.summary: Exchange an expiring session credential pair for a fresh one.
post.description: Presents the expired-but-signature-valid access credential in `Authorization: Bearer` and the renewal credential in the body. Both are required: the access credential establishes the tenant scope, the renewal credential authenticates. A client that has kept only one of the two cannot renew and its session is over. Renewal rotates — the credential presented here stops working, so store what comes back. Run at most one renewal at a time per client and retry the failed request after it returns.

refresh_credential.description: The renewal credential handed back by the previous renewal, or by the session open.

200.description: Renewed. The presented renewal credential is now retired.

access_credential.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer` on the session-credential routes.

refresh_credential.description: Shown once. Store it — the previous one no longer renews.

type.description: Problem-type URI; stays about:blank until a problem-type registry exists.

title.description: HTTP status reason phrase (never a leaked exception message).

code.description: Machine-readable UPPER_SNAKE classification consumers switch on. Deliberately an open string and NOT a $ref to ProblemCode: the closed per-condition taxonomy is published there, but this member also carries status-derived defaults and the derived INVALID_* validation codes, so constraining it here would make the spec reject responses this API really sends.

ProblemCode.description:
The per-condition problem codes — the finer-than-status taxonomy ADR-0025 reserves `code` for, carried by refusals implementing `Kernel\Exception\ProblemCoded`. This is the set worth branching on: two conditions can share a status and route a client to different screens (AUTH_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE and RECIPIENT_CANNOT_RECEIVE_METHOD are both 422 and mean opposite things — a deployment that cannot run the method, versus a contact detail the sender can fix in seconds).

⛔ NOT the whole value space of ProblemDetails.code, and treating it as closed will break you. Two other families reach the wire. (1) The status-derived defaults, which a refusal carries when it names no finer code: BAD_REQUEST, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, LOCKED, TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY, INTERNAL_ERROR, and ERROR as the last resort — a fixed set, listed here in full. (2) The validation family: VALIDATION_ERROR on the request-validation path, plus INVALID_* codes derived from the offending value's own type (INVALID_EMAIL, INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER, INVALID_TENANT_ID, …). That family is open by construction — the code is computed from a type name — so it is described rather than enumerated, because an enum that claimed to close it would be false.

▶ So: branch on the members below; for anything else, fall back to the HTTP status. An unknown code is expected, not a bug.

This list is generated from nothing — it is hand-maintained — but it cannot rot silently: OpenApiSpecTest asserts it equals the set of codes the ProblemCoded implementors actually carry, in BOTH directions, so a new code that is not published here fails the build, and so does an entry here that no refusal emits any more.

DeclaredAuthMethod.description: One method a recipient's gate declares, with where a code for IT would go (ADR-0054 §2.11). Referenced by both `methods` lists on GET /api/v1/signing/session/auth — the live gate's and the door's — because the two are the same shape and a second copy would be a second thing to keep true.

method.description: The declared method. Send this value as `method` on POST /signing/session/auth/otp/send to move the signer onto it.

masked_destination.description: Where a code for THIS method would be sent, masked server-side and handed over already masked — do not reconstruct it client-side. Null for a method that delivers nothing (eleven of the fifteen) and null when no contact of that shape is on file. ⚑ Showing it is the point of publishing the list: a signer who does not recognise a number can tell the sender BEFORE a code is sent to it.

code_length.description: Characters in the code for THIS method, so a segmented input can size itself. NULL means NOT KNOWABLE, never "no code" — same meaning as the top-level `code_length`.

FieldValueError.description: One field a commit's `filled_fields` got wrong — a record of `field_errors` on a `FIELD_VALUES_INVALID` refusal (ADR-0068). Every bad field is named at once, one code per field, sorted by `field_id`. ⛔ A record names the field and why, NEVER what was sent. `code` is a per-field term: it never appears as the response's own `code`. REQUIRED — a required field left blank, a required CHECKBOX left unticked. TOO_LONG — a TEXT over its `max_length` (32767 characters when none is authored), or, on a RESERVATIONS field, the commit's `reservations` over that field's `max_length`. CONTROL_CHARACTERS — a TEXT carrying a control character other than tab, line feed or carriage return. PATTERN_MISMATCH — a TEXT that breaks its pattern. INVALID_DATE — a DATE that is not a real day written YYYY-MM-DD. NOT_A_CHOICE — not the `value` of one of the field's choices. UNKNOWN_FIELD, READONLY, WRONG_TYPE — the client sent an entry it should not have (a field this recipient does not answer, a backend-forced field, a boolean for text or the other way round): a client defect, report it rather than showing it to the signer.

field_id.description: The refused field's id, lower-cased. Not always one the client sent: a REQUIRED record names a field the client left out, and a TOO_LONG on a RESERVATIONS field names the box that bounds `reservations`.

FilledField.description: One answer in a commit's `filled_fields`: exactly these two members.

field_id.description: The id of a field this recipient was shown and answers — a TEXT, DATE, CHECKBOX, DROPDOWN or RADIO field of theirs, not readonly.

value.description: A string for TEXT (as typed, not trimmed), DATE (YYYY-MM-DD) and DROPDOWN / RADIO (the chosen option's `value`); a boolean for CHECKBOX. `null` or "" is a blank. A number is refused.

Envelope.description: A single envelope projection (the GET response — mirrors EnvelopeJsonPresenter).

signing_mode.description: How the envelope is signed: one company seal over the finished document, or a real incremental PAdES signature per signing act (ADR-0034).

status.description: The phase of the lifecycle, never its result — read `outcome` for that. COMPLETED means the lifecycle ended, agreed or not (ADR-0073). VOIDED was retired: an envelope voided by its sender is SENT and closed while its last signatures land, then COMPLETED with `outcome: NOT_AGREED`. EXPIRED was retired too: an envelope past its `expires_at` ends as COMPLETED with `end_cause: EXPIRED` (or `outcome: AGREED`).

outcome.description: How the envelope came out, apart from its phase (ADR-0073): `AGREED` from the instant its agreement is secured — possibly while members are still pending — or `NOT_AGREED` from the instant it ends without agreement; null before either. An open enum: a value this list does not name reads as not fully agreed. `status: COMPLETED` alone never means agreed; read this.

end_cause.description: Why the envelope ended without agreement; null unless `outcome` is NOT_AGREED. SENDER_VOIDED names the actor in `ended_by`; RECIPIENT_DECLINED and RECIPIENT_VETOED name the recipient in `ended_by_recipient_id`; the others were decided by no party. Replaces `void_cause`: every envelope voided before this field existed carries SENDER_VOIDED or RECIPIENT_DECLINED.

agreed_at.description: When the agreement was secured: the admitted acts guarantee it whatever the members still pending do. From here a void is refused (ENVELOPE_REACHED_AGREEMENT). Null unless `outcome` is AGREED.

closed_at.description: When the envelope closed: no act is admitted from here. An ending without agreement closes at the decision; an agreement when its last step closes, or earlier when the sender closes it (`ended_by` set). The status stays SENT until every signature admitted before the close has landed. Replaces `voided_at`.

completed_at.description: When the lifecycle ended (`status: COMPLETED`), for either outcome.

ended_by.description: Qualified actor reference for whoever issued the sender-side act that closed the envelope: `client:<uuid>` for a machine client, `user:<uuid>` for a person (ADR-0046). Not a bare UUID -- the prefix is part of the value. Set by the sender's void (`outcome: NOT_AGREED`, `end_cause: SENDER_VOIDED`) or the sender's close-now (`outcome: AGREED`, `end_cause` null); null for every other ending. Read `outcome` for how the envelope ended, never `ended_by` alone. Replaces `voided_by`.

ended_by_recipient_id.description: The recipient whose decline or veto ended the envelope, when `end_cause` is RECIPIENT_DECLINED or RECIPIENT_VETOED; null otherwise. Replaces `voided_by_recipient_id`.

end_reason.description: The SENDER's optional reason given at void. Null for any other ending: a recipient's decline reason is on that recipient, as `decline_reason`. Replaces `void_reason`.

seal_pending_since.description: Derived: `closed_at` while the envelope is closed and its lifecycle has not ended (`status` is not COMPLETED); null otherwise. A closed envelope waits for every signature admitted before the close to land before it is sealed, so a signature that cannot yet be stamped holds it here; the value is when that wait began.

expires_at.description: When the envelope expires: its last deadline (ADR-0073). Null while a draft; resolved at the send as the send instant plus `expires_in_days`, and moved later only by an extension (POST …/expiry-extensions), never past 180 days after the send. From this instant the envelope admits no act and no sender action but that sweep: it closes within a minute, agreed if its open step already has what it needs and no later step is outstanding, otherwise NOT_AGREED with end_cause EXPIRED.

expires_in_days.description: The life the sender chose at creation, in days counted from the send (default 30). An extension moves `expires_at` and leaves this as chosen.

has_reservations.description: Derived: any recipient signed with an attest-with-exception reservation.

FieldPlacement.description: Rectangle in PDF points. The origin is the page's TOP-left and `origin_y` grows downward — the signing engine's convention (EU-DSS SignatureFieldParameters / pdf.js canvas), the opposite of PDF user space. One definition, referenced by the sender-facing and signer-facing field occurrences and by the retiring `document_assignments[].placements`: those are emitted by hand-written presenters in different bounded contexts that deptrac forbids from sharing code, so this schema is the only place the shape is stated once.

FieldOccurrence.description: One place a field appears: a document, and a rectangle on one of its pages. A field may appear several times, on one document or across several of the envelope's, and every occurrence shares ONE definition and ONE value (ADR-0041) — so a client prompts once per field and mirrors the answer into every rectangle. Composed from `FieldPlacement` by `allOf` so the geometry stays stated exactly once while the JSON is flat.

document_id.description: The document this rectangle sits on.

FieldOptions.description: Type-scoped configuration. Always present; both members are null far more often than not, and null means absent rather than empty — a rule that constrains nothing and a list with nothing to choose from are values the domain refuses to store.

choices.description: Options of a DROPDOWN / RADIO field, in rendering order. Values must be distinct. Null on a selection field is an ordinary DRAFT authoring state — the editor places the box before it fills the list — but an envelope cannot be *sent* holding one. Rejected on any other type.

value.description: What the answer carries when this option is picked.

label.description: What the signer reads on the option.

validation.description: Constraints a filled value must satisfy. Accepted on TEXT and DATE — every other type has a value space its own definition fixes — plus `max_length` alone on RESERVATIONS, where it bounds the committed reservations text. Applicability is also checked per member: `date_format` is DATE-only. On a DATE, `max_length` and `pattern` are accepted at authoring but applied by neither the signer nor the commit (BL-270): a date is judged as YYYY-MM-DD. On a TEXT, the commit applies `max_length` (32767 characters when none is authored) and `pattern`, the latter skipped exactly where the signer skips it — an over-long pattern or value, a nested quantifier, a pattern that does not compile here.

pattern.description: Regular expression in JavaScript syntax, run without flags and unanchored. Applied by the signer client and again at the commit, where a mismatch is a PATTERN_MISMATCH record and the rule is skipped exactly where the signer skips it. Keep to the subset a browser and PCRE agree on (BL-272).

pattern_message.description: Shown when `pattern` rejects the value. Requires `pattern`.

date_format.description: DATE only — rejected on TEXT, whose other validation members are accepted.

Field.description:
One thing a participant is asked for — a signature mark or a box they fill in, discriminated by `type` (ADR-0040) — and every place it appears (ADR-0041). Exactly one of `occurrences` / `anchor_text` is set: a text-tag field has no geometry until send-time resolution. There is no top-level `document_id`; a field's documents are its occurrences'.
THE ARRAY ORDER IS THE NAVIGATION ORDER: fields arrive as the envelope is read — document by document, page by page, top to bottom, left to right, taken from each field's earliest rectangle. There is no `ordinal`: a stored number had to be kept in step with the geometry by hand, and could not be right for two recipients who are shown different documents. A field with no geometry yet (a text tag) sorts last.

recipient_id.description: Null while authored but not yet assigned. Sending refuses a REQUIRED data field (TEXT, DATE, CHECKBOX, DROPDOWN, RADIO) that no recipient can reach — no recipient, or no rectangle on a document its recipient may read — and a data field assigned to a role that answers no fields. An optional field with no recipient may still be sent, and reaches nobody.

readonly.description: Backend-forced, never set at authoring. Always false today — the routing that would freeze a field after a prior signature is not built.

occurrences.description: Every rectangle this one field renders at, in authoring order, each naming its own document — one shared definition and one shared value across all of them. `null` (never `[]`) for a text-tag field until send-time resolution. A SIGNATURE field carries exactly one: one mark is one incremental PAdES signature (ADR-0034), so five marks are five fields, not one placed five times.

anchor_text.description: A {{Tag}} the send-time resolver turns into coordinates. ⚠ That resolver is NOT built, so a field authored this way never acquires geometry and the envelope cannot be sent — `POST /envelopes/{id}/send` refuses it with a 422. Accepted at authoring so the shape stays forward-compatible; use `occurrences` until then.

value.description: The answer the recipient's commit recorded for this field, once, at the commit: a string for TEXT (as typed), DATE (YYYY-MM-DD), DROPDOWN and RADIO (the chosen option's `value`); a boolean for CHECKBOX. Null until the recipient commits, null when they committed it blank, null when their commit collected no form at all, and always null on every other type. Read `filled_at` to tell those apart. A RESERVATIONS field holds no value of its own: it only places where the recipient's reservations are drawn, and their text is `recipients[].reservations`.

filled_at.description: On TEXT, DATE, CHECKBOX, DROPDOWN and RADIO: when the recipient's commit recorded this field — including a field they left blank, whose `value` stays null. Null while nothing is recorded, including after a commit that collected no form. Always null on every other type.

signed_at.description: On a SIGNATURE field only: the instant of that mark's own signature. Null on every other type — a data field's commit instant is `filled_at`, so "signed" never reads on a text box.

completion.description: How much agreement the step needs (ADR-0073): `ALL` — every blocking member signs; `AT_LEAST` — `min_signatures` of them. The reading of `min_signatures`, never stored apart from it: `ALL` exactly when it is null.

veto.description: Only ever true on an `AT_LEAST` step: one blocking member's decline, or a member never reached, ends the envelope not agreed.

deadline_hours.description: The step's deadline as authored, in hours from its activation; null for none. An `AT_LEAST` step without one waits for every member, and a veto step without one resolves only at the envelope's expiry.

deadline_at.description: The instant the deadline falls: `activated_at` plus `deadline_hours`. Null before the step activates, and for a step with no deadline.

auth.description: What this recipient must prove, and whether they are currently shut out. Each gate declares an ORDERED LIST since ADR-0054; the `*_method` scalars are the head of their list, kept because they are what every shipped client reads and derived so they cannot contradict it. A gate that asks nothing has `null` in the scalar and `[]` in the list. Both methods are null when nothing was declared: the link reaches the ceremony and nothing is asked at signing. `hard_locked` is true while a lockout bites; it clears the moment the sender calls the access-code or auth-unlock route. The access code itself is never returned by any read — it is surfaced exactly once, in the response of the call that minted it.

access_method.description: The FIRST method the access gate declares, or null when the door is open. Derived from access_methods, never stored beside it, so the two cannot disagree.

access_methods.description: Every method the access gate declares, in the sender's order (ADR-0054). The first is what the ceremony offers and, under the default escalation mode, sends. `[]` is the neutral — the door is open — and is always published, never null and never absent.

signing_method.description: The FIRST method the signing gate declares, or null when nothing is asked at the act. Derived from signing_methods.

signing_methods.description: Every method the signing gate declares, in order. An INDEPENDENT declaration from access_methods: a method the signer chose at the door reaches the act only if this list names it too.

selection.description: How this recipient meets their gates (ADR-0054 §2.4). ESCALATION — the first declared method is issued as soon as they open the ceremony and the rest unlock at the re-send cooldown. FREE_CHOICE — nothing is sent until the signer names a method. One value for the RECIPIENT, not one per gate, stated at add time and changed by no endpoint. Always present: a recipient nobody declared a mode for reads ESCALATION, which is a value rather than a gap. The SIGNER-facing descriptor publishes the same fact under the same two spellings, so a client reading both surfaces switches on one vocabulary.

locale.description: Language this recipient is written to in, as a BCP-47 tag. Written at add time and, on a recipient authored as a claimable slot, by the claim that fills it — the fill is the first moment the party's language is knowable at all, which is why it may carry one where a correction may not. A claim that omits it leaves the stored value untouched. No route edits it on a recipient already named: a correction moves where a party is reached, never who they are. `null` means nobody stated one — it is not a language, and notifications then follow the tenant default and, failing that, the platform default. A tag we author no copy in is accepted rather than rejected: the message is sent in the fallback language and records which language it actually used. Note there is no API for setting a tenant default yet, so in practice an unstated locale reaches the platform default; the platform default is currently Spanish.

outcome.description: This recipient's leg of the envelope: what the RECIPIENT did. Whether we could reach them is a different question and a different member — read `delivery` for that. `RELEASED` (ADR-0073): their leg was still open when something closed their part — the envelope ending, above all — and it closed without an act. `release_reason` says what the platform could prove about them, `released_by` what released them. No recipient is left PENDING on a closed envelope. ⛔ `DELIVERY_FAILED` was a member here until 2026-09-01 and is gone. It was never an outcome of the leg (it was explicitly non-terminal, so the step never closed over it): it annotated a leg that was still `PENDING`, and because it occupied this one field, a delivery failure erased the leg state it was annotating. A recipient we could not reach now reads `outcome: PENDING` with `delivery: FAILED`.

delivery.description: What we last observed about reaching this recipient, **per destination** — our channel's story, never a verdict on the signer. ⛔ A MAP keyed by contact point (`EMAIL_ADDRESS`, `MOBILE_PHONE`, `PHONE`), not a single value: a recipient can carry an address and a phone, and what happened to one says nothing about the other. An SMS the provider accepted does not mean the invitation email arrived. ⛔ `null`, or an ABSENT KEY, means **unknown** — not "nothing attempted". Nothing on the envelope side ever recorded a successful send before this member existed, and a destination nobody has tried supports no claim. A recipient whose email bounced and whose phone was never used publishes ONE key, not two. `FAILED` does not bar them from signing: the link is minted before delivery is attempted, so someone who got it another way completes normally. The recovery is `POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/corrections`, which forgets only the destination it actually changes. ⚠ `DELIVERED` is published so the vocabulary does not change shape later, and **nothing can produce it today**: every channel tops out at `SENT`, which means a provider accepted the message, not that it arrived.

observed_at.description: When the provider ACCEPTED (or refused) the message — the transmission, not when the send was requested. A delivery that goes out on a later retry carries that later instant. ⚠ Stable across redeliveries of the same observation, so it is safe to render directly; it does not creep.

signs_via.description: Where this recipient's signing act is performed. `SIGNING_PLATFORM` is the ordinary ceremony: they are sent a link and act here. `MACHINE_KEY` means a named integrator performs the act on their behalf over the machine surface, so they are never invited, no signing token is minted for them (`POST /signing-tokens` answers `RECIPIENT_SIGNS_ELSEWHERE`), and they never open anything. ⛔ Declared at authoring and never edited afterwards.

first_opened_at.description: When this recipient FIRST opened their signing link, or `null` if they never have. ⛔ For a `signs_via: MACHINE_KEY` recipient this stays `null` for ever, and that is the truth rather than a gap: nobody was sent a link and nobody opened one. Read the pair, not this field alone — otherwise a delegated party is indistinguishable from one who has not arrived yet. ⛔ `null` means "has not opened it" — never "unknown" — for every recipient including ones created before this field existed, which were backfilled from the signing sessions that had recorded the fact all along. So the absence is renderable, not just the presence. It is sealed once and never moves: reloads, a second device and a re-opened link all leave it at the first instant. Note it says the link was opened, not that the document was read. ⚑ An opening after the envelope closed (`closed_at`) is not recorded: it no longer counts as engaging with the envelope (ADR-0073), so a released informational recipient who comes back to read keeps `null` here.

authenticated_at.description: When this recipient FIRST passed their access gate, or `null` if they have not. ⚠ Where the access gate is open (`auth.access_methods` is `[]`) this is identical to `first_opened_at`, because passing an open gate IS arriving with the link — read `access_method_executed` to tell the two cases apart rather than comparing the timestamps. Sealed once: a recipient who re-authenticates after an idle session does not move it.

access_method_executed.description: What the authentication in `authenticated_at` actually executed, or `null` if the gate has not been passed. `DIRECT_LINK` means possession of the link and nothing more — the honest record of an open gate — so a client wanting "this person proved who they are" should test for a value OTHER than `DIRECT_LINK` rather than for presence. ⛔ This is what was executed, NOT what was declared: `auth.access_methods` is the sender's declaration, and the two differ whenever a signer chose a method further down the list. Frozen with `authenticated_at` at the first pass, so it does not track a later re-authentication.

reservations.description: Attest-with-exception note captured at signing (eCMR "recibí con incidencias"); null for a clean signature.

declined_at.description: When this recipient declined; null unless `outcome` is DECLINED (ADR-0070).

decline_reason.description: Why this recipient declined, in their own words, exactly as typed; null unless they declined. Never written into the document.

release_reason.description: What the platform could prove about a RELEASED recipient when it released them, first match (ADR-0073 §2.8): an informational member who never opened; a recipient the integrator acts for; one who passed the access gate and did not act; one whose latest invitation failed; an unclaimed slot; one never reached (step never activated, or no invitation sent); one whose invitation was sent and whose link had expired; one whose invitation was sent and whose link was valid. Decided at the release and never rewritten; a release by the deadline of a step or by the expiry is judged as of that deadline or `expires_at`, however late the scheduled sweep ran. Null unless `outcome` is RELEASED. An open enum.

released_by.description: What released the recipient: their step's deadline, the envelope's expiry, the sender closing a secured agreement, or the envelope closing otherwise (the envelope's `outcome` and `end_cause` say how). Null unless `outcome` is RELEASED. An open enum.

decline_access_method.description: The method the declining session had proved at the access gate — how the party who declined was identified. `DIRECT_LINK` means possession of the link and nothing more. Null unless they declined.

document_assignments.description: This recipient's relationship with each document of the envelope. Only what was declared: an empty list means nothing was declared, and there is no fan-out default on either axis (ADR-0034 §6, ADR-0039) — absence means no access. `sign` and `view` are two independent grants, not points on a scale: a party can be obliged to sign a carrier document they may not read.

sign.description: May this recipient sign the document.

view.description: May this recipient read the document.

placements.description: Where this recipient's signature renders. Empty = signed invisibly (cryptographically identical, simply not drawn). N placements means N incremental signatures. Never populated on a non-signing row.

SigningSession.description:
The recipient read-model the signer frontend renders `/view` from (ADR-0028).
Mirrors GetSigningSessionController::present(). Tenant, envelope and recipient
are derived from the bearer token — never sent by the client.

session_id.description: Deterministic UUIDv5 of (tenant, envelope, recipient) — not client-supplied.

status.description: DECLINED means this recipient declined their leg (POST /api/v1/signing/decline, ADR-0070). It is a SessionStatus member; INITIATED, AUTH_PENDING, AWAITING_REAUTH and REVOKED never reach this response.

envelope_outcome.description: How the ENVELOPE ended — AGREED or NOT_AGREED — or null while it has not closed. The same field, with the same values and the same null, as `envelope_outcome` on GET /api/v1/signing/session/auth: both are read from one rule. A fact about the whole envelope, never about this recipient — `status` says what happened to THIS participation. ⚠ null while the envelope is open, even once enough signatures are in to guarantee agreement: the envelope has not ended until it closes. A non-null value here means the envelope is over and what this response serves is the sealed copy — a read after the close waits for the seal, and is refused by name until it exists.

auth_requirements.description: What this recipient was asked to prove, one entry per declared gate. Empty when nothing was: the link reaches the ceremony and nothing is asked at signing, which is every envelope authored before ADR-0049.

authenticated.description: Whether the access gate has been passed. This route requires a session credential, so it is true whenever the route answers at all — a recipient who has not passed the gate holds no credential and is refused at the edge.

method_used.description: What this recipient ACTUALLY PROVED at the access gate — read from the session, never from the declaration (ADR-0054 §2.10). A gate may declare an ORDERED LIST and the signer may move down it, so this CAN differ from the first declared method: a recipient declared [OTP_EMAIL, OTP_SMS] who chose SMS reads OTP_SMS here while `auth_requirements[].method` still reads OTP_EMAIL. That is not a contradiction — one says what happened, the other what was asked — so do not derive either from the other. Two signers of one envelope may therefore reach different assurance levels. DIRECT_LINK is the honest record of the neutral pair: what was proved is possession of the link and nothing more.

name.description: Empty when the recipient is anonymous (addressed only by id).

email.description: Empty when the recipient is anonymous.

role.description: A `VIEWER` recipient is published here as `REVIEWER`: this app has no viewer term, and `REVIEWER` is the read-only role it drives a viewer with. So `REVIEWER` means "reads, does not sign", whichever of the two the sender authored. Non-signing roles (IN_PERSON_HOST, CERTIFIED_DELIVERY) never reach here — they are refused with 409 ROLE_NOT_INTERACTIVE.

allowed_signature_modes.description: The whole mode vocabulary, published forward so a client codes against it once. Live today: DRAW (biometric canvas) and TYPE (cursive font) — the only two the ceremony emits. Declared, not yet implemented: UPLOAD (image), VOCAL_BIOMETRIC (audio + voiceprint).

fields_draft.description: A partially-filled draft kept server-side between visits. Always null: no draft endpoint exists (BL-40), so a client keeps its draft locally and sends the final values on the commit, in `filled_fields`. What a commit recorded is each field's `current_value`.

download_url.description: Router-generated path to the document bytes (the chain tip).

page_count.description: Advisory — the backend does not parse the PDF; the viewer overrides it with the real count.

SigningField.description:
One thing the recipient must act on: a signature mark to produce, or an editable
field to fill in.

ONE ENTRY IS ONE ANSWER. A field printed on five pages — or on a contract and its
annex — arrives as a single entry carrying five `occurrences`, and the ceremony must
prompt for it ONCE and mirror the answer into every rectangle. Flattening the list
back into five entries re-creates exactly the defect ADR-0041 removed, where five
boxes held five independent values and five different tax ids were storable,
signable and sealable with nothing to object.

THE ARRAY ORDER IS THE NAVIGATION ORDER, and it is the only order signal on this
surface: entries arrive as this recipient reads them — document by document, page
by page, top to bottom, left to right, from each entry's earliest rectangle. Marks
and editable fields are INTERLEAVED by that order, not grouped by kind, so a mark
on page 1 precedes a text box on page 2. Present them in the order received.

Two sources for now. Marks are projected from a sender-authored placement — one
mark is one signature (ADR-0034), so N marks fan out to N entries, each with
exactly one occurrence — while editable fields come from `envelope.field`
(ADR-0040) and may carry several. That split is transitional; a `SIGNATURE` row of
`envelope.field` is deliberately NOT emitted here, so the two sources cannot render
the same box twice. Both collapse into one source when
`document_assignment_placement` retires.

Consequence for clients: `id` has two shapes. A mark's is synthesized as
`{document_id}-sig-{index}`; an editable field's is its real UUID. Do not assume
either — and note that only marks fan out, so a mark's id is not stable across a
re-authoring of the placement list.

`occurrences` is never empty here, unlike the sender-facing `Field`, which may
carry null geometry for a text-tag field. It may also be NARROWER than what the
sender authored: occurrences on documents this recipient may not see are withheld
(ADR-0039), while the value they enter still reaches all of them.

id.description: A field UUID, or `{document_id}-sig-{index}` for a placement-derived mark.

occurrences.description: Every rectangle to render for this one field. A mark always carries exactly one.

readonly.description: Backend-forced. Always false today — the routing that would freeze a field after a prior signature is not built.

current_value.description: The answer this recipient's commit recorded, once, at the commit (ADR-0040 Decision 6): a string for TEXT, DATE, DROPDOWN and RADIO, a boolean for CHECKBOX. Null until they commit, null for a blank, and always null on a signature mark. A draft being typed is never here — the final values travel on the commit's `filled_fields`. On a RESERVATIONS field it is the reservations text this recipient committed: render the reservations input at its occurrences, send the text in the commit's `reservations` — never in `filled_fields`, where a RESERVATIONS entry is refused — and bound it by the field's `max_length`.

expires_in_days.description: How long the envelope lives, in days, counted from the send — not from its creation: the send resolves it to `expires_at`, the envelope's last deadline. Optional, default 30, from 1 to 180. At `expires_at` the envelope stops admitting acts and closes within a minute: agreed if its open step already has what it needs and no later step is outstanding, otherwise not agreed with `end_cause: EXPIRED`. The sender may extend it later, up to 180 days after the send. A signing link lives seven days from its invitation whatever this is, so a life longer than that may need a resend; choose a life that fits the steps you expect.

completion.description:
How much agreement this step needs. `ALL` (the default): every blocking member (SIGNER, APPROVER) must sign, and one decline ends the envelope not agreed. `AT_LEAST`: `min_signatures` of them must sign; the others may decline or stay silent. Informational members (VIEWER, REVIEWER, EDITOR) never count and never hold a step. 

⚑ Unanimity has ONE encoding: send `ALL`. `AT_LEAST` with `min_signatures` equal to (or above) the step's blocking members is refused when the envelope is sent, with 422 `STEP_MINIMUM_NOT_BELOW_MEMBERS`. An `AT_LEAST` step also counts ONE blocking role: a step mixing SIGNER and APPROVER is refused at send with 422 `STEP_MIXES_BLOCKING_ROLES`. 

⚠ **An `AT_LEAST` step without `deadline_hours` waits for EVERY member**, not only for `min_signatures` of them: it closes when each blocking member has signed, declined or been released. So one that is not the last step should carry a deadline — otherwise a single silent member keeps the next step from ever activating, and the envelope ends not agreed at its expiry though the minimum was met. Accepted without one; this is the warning.

min_signatures.description: The `n` of `AT_LEAST n`: how many blocking members must sign. Required with `completion: AT_LEAST`, refused with `ALL`. At least 1, and below the number of blocking members the step ends up holding (checked when the envelope is sent, since recipients are added after the step). Read back under the same name on the step.

veto.description:
Only with `completion: AT_LEAST`. With a veto, one blocking member's decline ends the envelope not agreed (`RECIPIENT_VETOED`), and so does a member the platform never reached — never invited, invitation failed, or an unclaimed slot (`MEMBER_NOT_REACHED`) — since a veto step's premise is that everyone could object. A member invited whose link expired WAS reached, and their silence is no objection. 

⚠ **A veto step without `deadline_hours` resolves only at the envelope's expiry** when any member stays silent — the usual case on a board — and closing the envelope early is refused until then. Accepted without one; this is the warning.

deadline_hours.description: Optional deadline for this step, in hours from the moment the step activates (not from now): at least 24. When it passes, every blocking member of the step who has neither signed nor declined is released, the step closes and is judged on what was admitted, and an unclaimed slot of the step can no longer be claimed. Omit it (or send null) for no deadline: the step then waits for every member, or for the envelope's expiry.

AuthRequirementRequest.description: A recipient's two authentication gates. Each is declared EITHER as a single method (`access_method` / `signing_method`) OR as an ordered list (`access_methods` / `signing_methods`) — one spelling per slot, and sending both is a 422. Omit the object entirely, or leave a slot's scalar null and its list empty, for the default: the link reaches the ceremony and nothing further is asked at signing. `selection` is not a slot: it says how BOTH gates are presented to this recipient, and omitting it means ESCALATION, which is what every recipient does today.

access_method.description: What this recipient must prove to reach the ceremony at all. `null` (or omitted) leaves the door open: possession of the emailed link is enough, which is the behaviour every envelope has today. `DIRECT_LINK` is refused here — an open gate is said by omission, so that it has one spelling — and `MACHINE_KEY_ASSERTED` with it, which records how a delegated act was admitted and is declared on the recipient's `signs_via` instead. A method that cannot be established without a prior session is refused too, since this gate runs before any session exists. Both come back 422. A method this deployment has not wired is refused with 422 `AUTH_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE`; which methods those are differs per install, so read the code rather than assuming the published list is available. Send this OR `access_methods`, never both — they are two spellings of one declaration and the pair is refused with 422.

signing_method.description: What this recipient must prove at the moment of signing, bound to that act and consumed by it. `null` (or omitted) asks nothing further. Only methods that can issue a per-act challenge are accepted: `DIRECT_LINK`, `MACHINE_KEY_ASSERTED`, `VIDEO_KYC_ASYNC` and `CLAVE` are refused with 422 — the first issues nothing, the second records an act performed before this platform was involved, and the last two prove who someone is without naming the act. Independent of `access_method`, and not ranked against it: a strong identity at the door plus a short code per signature is a normal arrangement, not a contradiction. A method this deployment has not wired is refused with 422 `AUTH_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE`. Send this OR `signing_methods`, never both — the pair is refused with 422.

access_methods.title: The access gate's declaration as an **ordered list**, newest spelling.
access_methods.description: What this recipient must prove to reach the ceremony, as an ORDERED list. The first entry is what the ceremony offers — and, under the default escalation mode, actually sends — so the order is a decision about which channel is used first, and on SMS that is a decision about spend. The signer may then move down the list themselves; nothing on our side ever switches for them. A list of two or more may contain ONLY methods that deliver a code (`OTP_EMAIL`, `OTP_SMS`, `OTP_WHATSAPP`, `OTP_VOICE`): `ACCESS_CODE` is pre-shared out of band, so there is nothing to escalate to and mixing it with a delivered method would put two custodies in one slot. A list of ONE may name anything `access_method` could. Every method must also be one this deployment has wired (422 `AUTH_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE`) and one this recipient can actually receive (422 `RECIPIENT_CANNOT_RECEIVE_METHOD`) — the second is checked per member, so declaring SMS behind email still needs a phone. Repeats are refused. Send this OR `access_method`, never both.

signing_methods.title: The signing gate's declaration as an **ordered list**, newest spelling.
signing_methods.description: What this recipient must prove at the moment of signing, as an ORDERED list. Same rules as `access_methods`, and INDEPENDENT of it: the two gates are separate declarations that may name different sets, and a method the signer chose at the door starts this gate only if this list names it too. Send this OR `signing_method`, never both.

selection.title:
**How this recipient's gates are presented to them**
([ADR-0054](../../../../../../docs/adr/ADR-0054-ordered-auth-method-list.md) §2.4).
selection.description: How this recipient meets their gates. ESCALATION (the default, and what you get by omitting this) issues the FIRST declared method as soon as the signer opens the ceremony, and the rest become selectable when the re-send cooldown expires. FREE_CHOICE sends NOTHING until the signer names a method — the declared order then decides only what sits at the top of their list — because nobody should receive a code on a channel they did not choose, and on SMS that is a charge that bought nothing. ⛔ DO NOT SEND FREE_CHOICE UNTIL THE SIGNING APP RENDERS A CHOOSER: under it the code-send endpoint answers 409 AUTH_METHOD_NOT_CHOSEN when called with no `method`, which a client that does not know that code will treat as a broken link. One value for the recipient, not one per gate, and no endpoint changes it afterwards.

locale.description: Language this recipient is written to in, as a BCP-47 tag (`es`, `en`). Optional. Set it here, or - on a recipient you declare `claimable` - at the claim that fills the slot, which is the first moment the language of a party named later is knowable at all. A claim that omits it leaves whatever you set here alone. NO route edits it on a recipient who was named at authoring: the claim is refused on one with 409 `RECIPIENT_NOT_CLAIMABLE`, and the correction endpoint does not carry the field. Omit it (or send null) to leave it unstated, in which case the tenant default applies and, failing that, the platform default — though no API sets a tenant default yet, so today an unstated locale reaches the platform default, which is currently Spanish. A tag we author no copy in is accepted rather than rejected — the notification is sent in the fallback language and records which language it actually used.

phone.description: This recipient's phone number, in international format with its country code (`+34600123456`). Optional, and settable only here — the one endpoint that changes it afterwards is the correction. Stored canonicalised to E.164; spacing and punctuation you send are normalised away, so send it however you hold it. REQUIRED IN PRACTICE for a recipient you declare `OTP_SMS` on: a delivered code needs somewhere to go, and declaring the method without a number it can reach is refused here with 422 RECIPIENT_CANNOT_RECEIVE_METHOD rather than discovered when the signer is already waiting at a gate. A number that is not readable, or not assigned in its own numbering plan, is refused with 400 INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER. A Spanish landline is a valid number and is refused for OTP_SMS specifically, because it cannot receive a text.

access_code.description: A code the **sender** supplies, instead of letting the server generate one. Optional, and only meaningful when `auth.access_method` or `auth.signing_method` is `ACCESS_CODE`; sending it with neither gate declaring one is refused with 422, because there would be nothing to check it against. Minimum 6 characters. It is hashed immediately and **never stored, logged or returned** — supply it only when the signer already knows the value (the common case being a national id), since there is no way to read it back. Omit it and the server generates a 6-digit code, returned once in this call's 201 response and never again.

claimable.description:
Declares that this recipient is a SLOT deliberately authored without an occupant, to be named later through `POST /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/claim`. Default false, which is an ordinary recipient and is unchanged in every respect. 

What it changes: the contact check that would otherwise refuse this call with 422 `RECIPIENT_CANNOT_RECEIVE_METHOD` is DEFERRED rather than skipped — ALL of it, not the contact-absence cases alone. That is the whole check: OTP_EMAIL with no `email`, OTP_SMS with no `phone`, AND OTP_SMS against a landline, which is reachable here because nothing stops you sending a `phone` with `claimable: true`. The gate declaration is a policy and is knowable before the person is; whether it can be honoured is not. The same check, entire, with the same 422, is re-run at claim time against the contact the claim supplies. 

⚠ It defers NOTHING for an ordinary recipient: one you do not mark claimable and leave without a contact is refused here exactly as before. The deferral is keyed on this declaration and never on "has no contact yet".

signs_via.description: How this recipient's act reaches the platform. `SIGNING_PLATFORM` (the default, and what every recipient authored before this field existed is) means they sign through our own ceremony — hosted or embedded. `MACHINE_KEY` means a named integrator holding a machine API key performs the act for them and asserts it authenticated them in its own system; that party never opens a link and is never sent one. ⛔ This is NOT an authentication method and does not belong in either gate: `MACHINE_KEY` REQUIRES the neutral pair — omit `auth` entirely, or send it with neither gate declared — and any other combination is refused with 422, because a declared gate says this recipient must prove something to us while a delegated act says they will never appear, and an envelope carrying both can be signed by nobody.

CorrectRecipientRequest.description: At least one of `email` or `phone` must be present. A field you omit is left as it is — there is no way to clear a contact through this endpoint.

email.description: The corrected email address for this recipient. Replaces the address on file and returns the recipient to PENDING, after which a fresh invitation is sent to it — at once if their step is already active, otherwise when their step opens. OMIT IT (or send null) to leave the address on file untouched and correct only the phone; omitting BOTH is refused with 422. Each recipient may be corrected at most 3 times — a correction that is REFUSED spends nothing — and the 4th successful attempt is refused with 409 RECIPIENT_CORRECTION_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, past which the recovery is to void the envelope and reissue it.

phone.description: The corrected phone number, in international format with its country code (`+34600123456`). Stored canonicalised to E.164; spacing and punctuation you send are normalised away. OMIT IT to leave the number on file untouched. A number that is not readable, or not assigned in its own numbering plan, is refused with 400 INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER. A number that is valid but cannot carry a method this recipient has declared — correcting a mobile to a landline while OTP_SMS is declared — is refused with 422 RECIPIENT_CANNOT_RECEIVE_METHOD, and the correction is NOT spent.

access_code.description: A replacement code the **sender** supplies, instead of letting the server generate one. Optional — omit it (or send `{}`) and the server mints a 6-digit code from a CSPRNG, which is the usual case. Minimum 6 characters. It is hashed immediately and **never stored, logged or returned**; supply it only when the signer already knows the value. Either way the previous code stops working the moment this call succeeds, and any lockout the recipient was under is lifted with it.

ClaimRecipientRequest.description: Names the party a claimable slot was authored without. `full_name` is required; the contact members are required only insofar as the gates DECLARED on this recipient need somewhere to deliver — OTP_EMAIL needs `email`, OTP_SMS needs a mobile `phone`, and a gate naming both needs both. Nothing is required for being a claim. A slot is filled ONCE: an identical replay of this body returns the same 204 as the first call, and a body that diverges on a field it supplies is refused with 409.

full_name.description: The name of the party this slot is being filled with. REQUIRED on every claim, including one whose declared gates need no contact at all: the fill happens once and cannot be repeated, so a claim naming nobody would settle the slot empty and permanently. This is the answer to "who was this envelope addressed to?", and it is the one member of this body that is never derived from the gates.

email.description: The email address the claimed party is reached at. Optional in the shape and REQUIRED IN PRACTICE whenever this recipient declares OTP_EMAIL — the destination check the authoring call deferred is re-run here, against what this body supplies, and refuses with 422 RECIPIENT_CANNOT_RECEIVE_METHOD when a declared method has nowhere to go. ⚑ A REFUSED claim consumes none of the once-only fill, so fixing the body and retrying is free.

phone.description: The phone number the claimed party is reached at, in international format with its country code (`+34600123456`). Stored canonicalised to E.164; spacing and punctuation you send are normalised away. REQUIRED IN PRACTICE whenever this recipient declares OTP_SMS. A number that is not readable, or names no assigned range, is refused with 400 INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER; a Spanish landline is a perfectly valid number and is refused for OTP_SMS specifically with 422 RECIPIENT_CANNOT_RECEIVE_METHOD, because it cannot receive a text.

locale.description: Language the claimed party is written to in, as a BCP-47 tag (`es`, `en`). Optional. ⚑ The claim is the FIRST moment this is knowable at all — the party did not exist when the slot was authored — which is why a fill may carry it where the correction endpoint deliberately may not. Omit it (or send null) to leave it unstated, in which case the tenant default applies and, failing that, the platform default. A tag we author no copy in is accepted rather than rejected: the notification goes out in the fallback language and records which one it used.

reason.description: Why you are cancelling the envelope. This text is NOT an internal note: it is quoted verbatim to the recipients, in the notice every recipient the platform has already invited receives when the envelope is cancelled. Write it for them. It is also recorded on the envelope (`end_reason`) and in the envelope's event log. Omit it, send null, or send an empty or whitespace-only string to cancel without a reason: the recipients then get the notice without one. Notices go by email today and carry the reason in full; should they ever go by SMS, the reason may be shortened there to fit a single message.
reason.example: The terms changed; we will send you an updated contract this week.

expires_at.description: The new `expires_at`, as an RFC 3339 instant: after the current one, and no later than 180 days after the envelope was sent.

resend.title:
`true` re-sends: a new code is minted and **the one already in the signer's inbox stops
working**. `false`, or absent, ensures a live code exists without disturbing one that does.

recover.title:
`true` asks to face the **access** gate again on a session that has already passed it — the
recovery of [ADR-0053](../../../../../../docs/adr/ADR-0053-access-grant-recovery.md), for a client
that has lost its credential pair (a mobile tab discarded in the background takes
`sessionStorage` with it).
recover.description:
⛔ **Absent means *no*, and the default direction is the safe one for the same reason `resend`'s
is.** This is not a field to set on component mount: sent unconditionally it would ask an
authenticated signer to re-type a code they already proved, on every load. Send it only from a
deliberate *"I have lost my session"* control, or when the open route answered `AUTH_PASSED`
with no `access_credential` — which is exactly the stranded state, and is the only way a client
can tell.

⚑ **It grants nothing by itself.** It changes which gate the server asks about; the answer must
still be right, a wrong one still spends the guessing budget, and both lockout tiers and the
send limiter apply unchanged.

method.title:
**Which declared method to use** — the signer moving down the gate's ordered list
([ADR-0054](../../../../../../docs/adr/ADR-0054-ordered-auth-method-list.md) §2.5–§2.7).
method.description: Which of the methods this recipient's gate declares to send the code on — the signer moving down the ordered list (ADR-0054). OMIT IT for the current behaviour: the server uses whatever is in force, which is the gate's first method until the signer has chosen. ⛔ SENDING IT IS A SELECTION AND A SELECTION MINTS: the code already in the inbox stops working and a new one goes out on the named channel, so it obeys the same 60-second minimum interval as `resend` — changing channel does NOT restart the cooldown, and `next_resend_at` is when both become possible. ⚑ Naming the method that is ALREADY live is the one exception: nothing is minted and the live code keeps working, so a re-mount that repeats the choice is safe. A method the gate does not declare is refused with 409 `AUTH_METHOD_NOT_DECLARED` — it is never silently replaced by the first one. Read the declared list from GET /api/v1/signing/session/auth.

code.title: The code the signer typed.
code.description:
⚠ The upper bound is a denial-of-service guard, not a policy statement: it caps what reaches the
hasher. It is deliberately far above any real code length so it can never be read as the
accepted format.

`true` asks to face the **access** gate again on a session that has already passed it — the
recovery of [ADR-0053](../../../../../../docs/adr/ADR-0053-access-grant-recovery.md), for a client
that has lost its credential pair (a mobile tab discarded in the background takes
`sessionStorage` with it).

⛔ **Absent means *no*, and the default direction is the safe one for the same reason `resend`'s
is.** This is not a field to set on component mount: sent unconditionally it would ask an
authenticated signer to re-type a code they already proved, on every load. Send it only from a
deliberate *"I have lost my session"* control, or when the open route answered `AUTH_PASSED`
with no `access_credential` — which is exactly the stranded state, and is the only way a client

⚑ **It grants nothing by itself.** It changes which gate the server asks about; the answer must
still be right, a wrong one still spends the guessing budget, and both lockout tiers and the

asserted_document_hashes.title:
⛔ **A map of `documentId => digest`, covering EXACTLY the documents this recipient signs.**
Fewer is a signatory who did not see everything they signed; more names a document they were
not asked to sign. Both are refused, and the refusal names the document.

filled_fields.title:
What the integrator asserts the recipient answered — or absent when it collected no form. The
same member, meaning and shape as on the recipient's own route (TASK-044 §4 D8).

What the recipient answered in the form they were shown — or absent when this client showed
no form (TASK-044 §3 #1, §4 D15). Shape only here; see {@see \F5Sign\Session\UI\Http\Request\FilledFieldsShape}.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request or missing tenant scope.

Unauthorized.description: No credential this route accepts: missing, unrecognised, or no longer valid. Carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`. Deliberately does not distinguish the cases.

NotFound.description: Resource not found (or not visible to the requesting tenant).

Conflict.description: The resource is not in a state that permits the action (e.g. voiding a non-voidable envelope).

UnprocessableEntity.description: Validation failed; `errors` lists the offending fields.

ServiceUnavailable.description: `ENVELOPE_BUSY` — another write to the same envelope held a lock this request needed for longer than the request was willing to wait. Nothing about the request was wrong: retry it after the `Retry-After` delay. Transient by construction; a client that shows it as a failure of the user's action is showing the wrong thing.

DeclaredSubjectHeader.name: F5Sign-Declared-Subject
DeclaredSubjectHeader.description: Which human triggered this request, declared by you. An API key names an *organisation*, so the person behind a call is not proven by the credential — this value is recorded beside the fact and is never treated as the actor. Send an opaque, integrator-scoped reference to the person (something meaningful only inside your own system), or exactly `f5s:none` when no human triggered the request. Must not be an email address or a name: at most 128 octets, no whitespace, no `@`. The `f5s:` prefix is reserved. Absent, empty or malformed answers 400.

machineApiKey.description: Machine API key issued by `app:identity:provision-api-client`. Shown once at issuance and never recoverable. Unauthenticated requests to a machine route answer 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.

signingToken.description: The recipient signing token carried by the emailed link. Admits opening a signing session and nothing beyond it: the read-model, the document bytes and the commit require the session credential a passed gate mints. Presenting this token on those routes is refused, not retried against the other verifier.

sessionCredential.description: Returned when a signing session is opened, and again by every renewal. Fifteen minutes. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer` on the recipient read-model, the document bytes and the commit. It REPLACES the emailed token on those routes rather than accompanying it — one credential per request.
